title: Hall, yard and zones overview
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates from a single-storey warehouse hall of 6,000 m2 in Port Sellow, with 10 m clear height under roof. A small office annex is attached to the hall for administration, dispatch and supervision. All storage, handling and value-added activities take place inside this one hall.

2. Outside the hall is a fenced yard of approximately 3,500 m2. The yard contains the dock apron, manoeuvring area for trailers, marked pedestrian routes and the marked driver waiting area. Drivers remain in the waiting area and do not enter the hall. Access to the yard and to dock doors is controlled by the dispatcher.

3. The building is served by 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, each equipped with its own leveller. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and serve receiving. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and serve dispatch. Every carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot by the dispatcher before arrival.

4. The hall floor is divided into six fixed zones, A to F, which all staff must know. The zones have fixed functions, fixed boundaries and fixed sizes. Goods move between zones only in the defined sequence and only after release from the previous zone.

5. Zone A — receiving, 800 m2, is located at inbound docks 1-4. It is used for unloading, document checking, counting and goods inspection. No inbound goods leave Zone A until paperwork has been checked and the goods have been inspected.

6. Zone B — bulk storage, 2,200 m2, is the high-bay pallet store with 2,400 pallet positions. It holds reserve stock for replenishment of picking and cold storage. Zone C — picking, 1,200 m2, holds ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from Zone B. It is the only zone where customer orders are picked.

7. Zone D — dispatch, 900 m2, is the outbound staging area in front of outbound docks 5-8. Only wrapped and labelled pallets staged for an assigned door are held here. Zone E — cold zone, 300 m2, is the chilled store held between +2 °C and +8 °C. Zone F — services and control, 600 m2, contains value-added packing, quarantine, returns inspection and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2.

8. Main transport aisles through the hall are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Pedestrian walkways are physically separated by yellow barriers, are 1.2 m wide, and must be used for all movement on foot. Speed limits, dock discipline and pedestrian rules apply throughout the hall and yard and are detailed in Chapter 10.

title: Shifts and supervision
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates Monday to Friday on a fixed two-shift system. All regular receiving, storage, picking, packing and dispatch activities take place within these shifts. There is no regular night operation and no regular weekend operation.

2. The morning shift runs from 06:00 to 14:00. The afternoon shift runs from 14:00 to 22:00. Shift start and end times are fixed and apply to all floor staff, including forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, dispatchers and floaters.

3. Between 06:00 and 22:00 on working days the site is continuously staffed and supervised. Outside these hours the hall is closed, dock doors are secured, and no handling, loading or unloading takes place unless approved overtime is in effect.

4. Each shift is run by one designated shift supervisor. There are two shift supervisors in total, one for mornings and one for afternoons. At any time during operating hours there is always exactly one shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

5. The shift supervisor directs all floor staff during the shift, allocates tasks within the shift plan, ensures zone discipline and procedure compliance, and leads the immediate response to any incident, damage, spill or evacuation. Instructions from the shift supervisor on duty are binding for all floor staff.

6. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site across both shifts, for operations, safety and final sign-offs. The shift supervisors report to the warehouse manager. Matters that exceed the authority of the shift supervisor, including overtime, stocktake sign-off and write-offs above 500 EUR, are escalated to the warehouse manager.

7. Around 38 to 40 people are employed on site in total, distributed across the two shifts to maintain receiving at doors 1-4, bulk storage and replenishment, picking, packing and dispatch at doors 5-8, plus stock control, maintenance and dispatch functions. Floater staff cover absence so that supervision and key functions are never left uncovered during operating hours.

8. In peak season additional capacity is provided by Saturday morning overtime only. Saturday overtime is limited to the morning hours, is planned in advance, and is used for backlog clearance, replenishment and outbound preparation. There is no regular Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday working.

9. Overtime is approved only by the warehouse manager. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and other staff cannot authorise overtime. No employee works outside the Monday to Friday shift times or on Saturday without prior written approval from the warehouse manager.

10. Continuity between shifts is maintained through a documented end-of-shift handover from the outgoing shift supervisor to the incoming shift supervisor in accordance with PR-15. The handover ensures that dock bookings, open inbound and outbound loads, replenishment status, quarantine and hazmat status, and any incidents are transferred with clear ownership at 14:00 and at 22:00.

title: General floor rules and PPE
text:
1. Access to the warehouse floor is permitted only with mandatory personal protective equipment. Every person on the warehouse floor must wear a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times, with no exceptions. This applies to all employees, supervisors and managers, as well as to any authorised visitor or contractor while on the floor.

2. High-visibility vests must be worn closed and visible, not covered by other clothing or carried in the hand. Class S3 safety footwear must be worn correctly laced and in serviceable condition. Any person without the required vest and footwear must leave the floor immediately and report to the shift supervisor. Work does not start or continue without full PPE.

3. Forklift operators and drivers of any other materials handling equipment must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. The seat belt must be fastened before moving off and must remain fastened until the truck is fully stopped and secured. No truck is operated without a fastened seat belt, and non-compliance is stopped by the shift supervisor.

4. All movement on foot inside the hall must use the physically separated pedestrian walkways and marked crossings. The walkways are 1.2 m wide and are protected by yellow barriers. Pedestrians must not take shortcuts through transport aisles, rack storage aisles, dock areas or staging zones, and must not step outside barriers into truck routes.

5. Pedestrians have priority in all marked pedestrian zones, at crossings and on the dock ramps. Powered trucks must reduce speed to 5 km/h in these areas and stop where required under PR-10 and PR-11. Pedestrians must still make eye contact with the driver and wait until the truck has stopped before crossing.

6. The general speed limits apply to all powered trucks and are enforced. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and they must be kept clear of pallets, waste and obstructions at all times.

7. Drivers and external carriers are not permitted in the hall. Drivers wait only in the marked waiting area in the yard until called to their assigned door and time slot. Inbound work uses doors 1-4 and outbound work uses doors 5-8, as assigned by the dispatcher. No loading or unloading takes place at any other door.

8. Zone discipline is a basic safety rule. Nothing moves past Zone A until paperwork has been checked, and only inspected and booked goods go to put-away in Zone B, E or F. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are held in Zone D. Hazmat is stored only in the ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F. Damaged goods go to quarantine the same day they are found.

9. All floor activities follow the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15. If a procedure, instruction or supervisor direction conflicts with safe practice, work must stop and the shift supervisor must be informed immediately. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor directs incident response, and instructions on safety, PPE and evacuation are binding for everyone on site.

title: Roles on the floor
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. employs around 38 to 40 people on site. The organisation is flat and role-based, so that every activity on the floor has a clear owner on each shift. All staff work within the Monday to Friday two-shift system, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only.

2. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site. This includes all operations from receiving to dispatch, occupational safety, inventory accuracy, and all final sign-offs. The warehouse manager sets the shift plan, approves overtime, and is the only person who can authorise new forklift operators.

3. Two shift supervisors run the floor, one on the morning shift from 06:00 to 14:00 and one on the afternoon shift from 14:00 to 22:00. There is always exactly one shift supervisor in charge of the floor during operating hours. The shift supervisor directs floor staff, enforces zone discipline and procedures PR-01 to PR-15, and leads immediate incident response.

4. Eight forklift operators carry out all powered handling. They drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks and electric pallet jacks, and also use hand pallet jacks for small moves. They perform put-away to Zone B, E and F, replenishment of pick faces in Zone C, staging to Zone D, and loading and unloading at the dock doors. No other role operates forklifts or reach trucks.

5. Six inbound operators staff Zone A at inbound docks 1-4. They receive carriers at the assigned door and time slot, check documents before unloading, unload, count and inspect goods, and prepare inspected goods for system booking and release to put-away. Nothing moves past Zone A without their document check and inspection.

6. Ten pickers work in Zone C. They pick customer orders against WMS scanner tasks using the handheld scanners, scan-verify every picked item, and feed packed and labelled goods to Zone D. Picking takes place only in Zone C on ground-level pick faces and flow racks, and only against an active scanner task.

7. Two stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day. They run the daily cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule, perform second counts and recounts, investigate discrepancies between system stock and rack stock, and prepare adjustments for approval. They also prepare the annual wall-to-wall stocktake for sign-off by the warehouse manager.

8. Four returns and packing staff work in Zone F and in packing. In Zone F they inspect returns and propose restock, rework or scrap for approval. In value-added packing they carry out packing, labelling and rework tasks, and operate the stretch wrappers and cardboard baler as instructed. They also place damaged goods into quarantine on the day damage is found.

9. Two dispatchers control transport and doors. They book transport, assign every carrier a door and time slot, manage the driver waiting area discipline, and release outbound loads from Zone D at docks 5-8. Inbound work is assigned only to doors 1-4 and outbound work only to doors 5-8. The dispatchers do not authorise overtime and do not approve write-offs.

10. One maintenance technician maintains trucks, racking and dock equipment. This covers the electric fleet, chargers, racking, dock levellers, stretch wrappers, baler and scanners. Every repair is logged, and racking is subject to documented monthly safety inspection. Faults affecting safety or load capacity are reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the warehouse manager.

11. Two floaters cover absence across roles. They are trained for inbound support, picking, packing and pallet-jack moves, so that receiving, replenishment, picking and dispatch never lose cover during operating hours. When covering a task they work under the direction of the shift supervisor and follow the same procedure as the role owner.

title: Approvals and ownership
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site and owns all operations, safety and inventory accuracy. This accountability cannot be delegated. The warehouse manager gives the final sign-offs for the site and is the escalation point for every matter that exceeds the authority of the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

2. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime. No Saturday morning overtime in peak season, no extension of the Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, and no work outside operating hours takes place without prior written approval from the warehouse manager. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and other staff cannot authorise overtime.

3. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators. No licence, no truck: no employee operates the 2.5 t counterbalance forklifts, 1.6 t reach trucks or electric pallet jacks without this personal authorisation. The authorisation is recorded and is a precondition for any truck assignment by the shift supervisor.

4. The warehouse manager signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results. The stocktake is prepared by the stock controllers on the basis of full counts, second counts and documented recounts, but the result becomes binding only with the signature of the warehouse manager. No stocktake is closed without this sign-off.

5. Write-off authority is fixed by a 500 EUR threshold. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case. Any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No write-off is split to stay below the threshold, and every write-off is documented with cause, quantity, value and disposition.

6. The shift supervisor owns the floor during the shift. The supervisor on duty directs all floor staff, enforces zones A-F discipline and procedures PR-01 to PR-15, allocates tasks within the shift plan, and leads immediate incident response. Instructions from the shift supervisor on duty on safety, PPE, zone stops and evacuation are binding for everyone on site.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Any damage, near miss, spill, rack impact, truck fault, temperature alarm or personal injury is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty, who secures the area, initiates response under the relevant procedure, and reviews and countersigns the report. Reports requiring decisions above supervisor authority are escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift.

8. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns. Returns staff in Zone F inspect every returned unit within the 14-day acceptance rule and propose restock, rework or scrap, but goods are not restocked, reworked or scrapped without the recorded approval of the shift supervisor. Damaged goods found at any stage go to quarantine the same day under PR-09.

9. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling and outbound release. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot, controls the driver waiting area, and enforces the split of doors 1-4 inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only. No truck is loaded, unloaded or moved to a door without dispatcher assignment, and no outbound load leaves Zone D without dispatcher release under PR-06.

10. Day-to-day ownership is fixed by role. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy, daily cycle counts, second counts and adjustment preparation, with no adjustment posted without a second count. The maintenance technician owns the condition of trucks, racking and dock equipment and logs every repair, with monthly documented racking inspections. Inbound operators own the Zone A document check, and pickers own scan-verified picking in Zone C only against active scanner tasks.

title: Procedure system PR-01 to PR-15
text:
1. All work at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. runs off fifteen written procedures, PR-01 to PR-15. The procedures are binding for every role on the floor and in the yard. No receiving, storage, picking, packing, dispatch, counting or maintenance task is performed outside its procedure, and instruction from a supervisor does not replace a procedure.

2. The procedures follow the physical flow of goods through zones A to F. PR-01 Inbound receiving covers carrier arrival at doors 1-4, document checking before unloading, unloading, counting and inspection in Zone A. PR-02 Put-away to storage covers booking into the system and transfer of inspected goods only to Zone B, E or F. PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces covers feeding Zone C from bulk storage before each picking shift.

3. PR-04 Order picking covers picking in Zone C only, against WMS scanner tasks, with scan-verification of every picked item. PR-05 Packing and labelling covers packing, labelling, wrapping on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers and transfer to Zone D. PR-06 Outbound dispatch covers staging of wrapped and labelled pallets only in Zone D, dispatcher release, and loading and sealing at doors 5-8.

4. PR-07 Returns handling covers acceptance of returns within 14 days of delivery, inspection of every unit in Zone F, and proposal of restock, rework or scrap for shift supervisor approval. PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts covers daily cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule, second counts before any adjustment, and the annual wall-to-wall stocktake signed off by the warehouse manager.

5. PR-09 Damaged-goods handling covers quarantine on the same day damage is found, inspection, write-off within the 500 EUR authority rule, and final disposition. PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation covers authorisation, daily checks before first use, charging, and safe driving of the 2.5 t counterbalance forklifts, 1.6 t reach trucks, electric and hand pallet jacks. PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse covers walkways, barriers, crossings and priority rules.

6. PR-12 Cold-chain handling covers storage in Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C, alarms, manual temperature verification each shift, and put-away and replenishment discipline for chilled goods. PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response covers storage only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F up to 4,000 kg, handling limits, and spill containment and reporting.

7. PR-14 Emergency evacuation covers alarms, escape routes, quarterly drills, and roll call at the assembly point by the north fence before any re-entry. PR-15 End-of-shift handover covers the documented transfer at 14:00 and 22:00 from the outgoing to the incoming shift supervisor, including dock bookings, open loads, replenishment, quarantine and hazmat status, and incidents.

8. Ownership of the procedures is fixed. The warehouse manager owns the system as a whole and approves any new version. The shift supervisor enforces PR-01 to PR-15 on the floor and stops any work that deviates from them. Stock controllers own PR-08 in daily execution, dispatchers own PR-06 scheduling and release, and the maintenance technician supports PR-10, PR-13 and PR-14 for equipment readiness.

9. If a procedure cannot be followed, work stops and the shift supervisor is informed immediately. The goods or equipment stay where they are, the area is secured, and the deviation is recorded as an incident. Only the warehouse manager can approve a temporary departure from a procedure, and only with a documented instruction and compensating safety measure.

10. The fifteen procedures are trained on day one for zone discipline, PPE and pedestrian rules, and thereafter by role before any unsupervised work. Only authorised forklift operators work under PR-10, only inbound operators under PR-01, only pickers under PR-04, and only returns staff under PR-07 and PR-09. Floaters follow the procedure of the role they cover.

title: Carrier arrival and dock assignment
text:
1. All inbound transport arrives only on the basis of a prior booking by the dispatcher. Every carrier is assigned a specific inbound door from doors 1-4 and a fixed time slot before arrival. No truck arrives unannounced, no truck chooses its own door, and no inbound truck is directed to outbound doors 5-8.

2. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. The dispatcher books transport, fixes the sequence of inbound arrivals for the shift, balances doors 1-4 against unloading capacity in Zone A, and coordinates with outbound work at doors 5-8 so that yard movements do not conflict. The shift supervisor does not change door assignments without agreement from the dispatcher.

3. Carriers must arrive within their assigned time slot and report to the yard entrance on arrival. The driver announces the booking reference, client, load and assigned door. Early or late arrivals do not proceed to a door automatically but wait for a revised instruction from the dispatcher. Double-booked or unbooked arrivals are held outside the dock apron until clarified.

4. After reporting, the driver moves the vehicle only to the marked waiting area in the fenced yard of 3,500 m2 and waits there until called to the door. Drivers remain in the waiting area and never enter the hall. The waiting area is the only permitted place for drivers to wait, rest and prepare documents before docking.

5. Movement in the yard is controlled and speed-limited. The general limit in the yard is 15 km/h, reduced to 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Trailers manoeuvre only on the marked manoeuvring area and dock apron under direction of the dispatcher and the shift supervisor.

6. The call to the door is given by the dispatcher when Zone A and the assigned door are ready. Only then does the driver leave the waiting area and reverse to the assigned door at doors 1-4. Each dock door is at 1.2 m dock height and has its own leveller, which is operated only by trained inbound or forklift staff, never by the driver.

7. On docking, the driver secures the vehicle, switches off the engine where required, hands over the transport documents from the cab or waiting area interface, and returns to the waiting area. Drivers do not take part in unloading, counting or inspection, do not enter Zone A, and do not walk through the yard outside the marked pedestrian routes.

8. Inbound docks 1-4 are used exclusively for receiving. No outbound staging, loading or sealing takes place at these doors, and no outbound pallets are held in Zone A. If all inbound doors are occupied, arriving trucks continue to wait in the waiting area and are not staged on transport aisles, pedestrian walkways or the dock apron.

9. The shift supervisor ensures readiness of Zone A for each booked arrival, with inbound operators, forklifts or pallet jacks and WMS scanners available at the assigned door. Delays, door faults, leveller faults or congestion in Zone A are reported immediately to the dispatcher, who re-sequences time slots and informs waiting drivers.

10. Every arrival, time-slot deviation, door change and waiting time is recorded by the dispatcher and transferred in the end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Open inbound loads, trucks still in the waiting area at 14:00 and 22:00, and rebooked slots are handed over with clear ownership, so the incoming shift and supervisor know which carrier is at which door and which truck is still waiting.

title: Documents, unloading and inspection
text:
1. No inbound goods are unloaded before the transport documents have been checked and released in Zone A. The document check is the mandatory first step of PR-01 Inbound receiving and is owned by the inbound operators. Unloading starts only after the check is recorded as passed for that truck and door.

2. The inbound operator at the assigned door from doors 1-4 verifies the delivery note, client and purchase or inbound order, pallet and carton quantities, product identities, batch or expiry data where applicable, and cold-chain or hazmat papers where applicable. The booking reference, carrier and time slot assigned by the dispatcher must match the arriving vehicle.

3. If documents are missing, incomplete, or do not match the booking, unloading does not start. The goods and vehicle stay at the door, the area is held clear, and the inbound operator informs the shift supervisor and the dispatcher immediately. The dispatcher clarifies with the carrier or client, and the decision to hold, partially receive or refuse the load is recorded before any further handling.

4. After document release, unloading is carried out by trained forklift operators and inbound operators using the electric fleet and hand pallet jacks. The dock leveller at the 1.2 m door is operated only by trained warehouse staff. Drivers do not take part in unloading and do not enter Zone A or the hall.

5. All unloaded goods remain in Zone A for counting and inspection. Nothing moves past Zone A to Zone B, E or F until counting and inspection are complete. Pallets are placed only in the marked Zone A lanes, transport aisles and pedestrian walkways are kept clear, and the 8 km/h hall limit and 5 km/h limit at pedestrian zones and ramps are observed.

6. Every delivery is counted pallet by pallet and, where required, carton by carton against the checked documents. Counts are performed by the inbound operators and confirmed with WMS scanners. Shortages, overages and mislabelled pallets are segregated within Zone A, marked as pending, and reported to the shift supervisor before booking.

7. Every delivery is inspected in Zone A before booking. Packaging integrity, pallet condition, labelling, visible damage, contamination, and expiry or temperature indicators are checked. Chilled goods are checked for cold-chain evidence and directed under PR-12, and hazmat packages are checked for labelling, closure and leakage and held for the Zone F cage procedure under PR-13.

8. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods are not booked as available stock and are not put away to bulk storage. They are marked, segregated in Zone A, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. The finding, quantity and door are recorded for the incident review and for the end-of-shift handover under PR-15.

9. Only goods that have passed document check, count and inspection are released for system booking and put-away. Release is recorded by door, delivery and pallet, with shortages, damages and quarantine transfers noted. Unreleased goods stay under the control of the inbound operators in Zone A until the discrepancy is resolved or the goods are refused.

10. Zone A is cleared by delivery so that the next booked carrier can dock. Inspected and released pallets are staged for prompt collection to Zone B, E or F, quarantine transfers are completed the same day, and paperwork, counts and inspection results are handed over for booking. No inbound load is left unassigned at shift change at 14:00 and 22:00.

title: Booking and release to put-away
text:
1. Only goods that have passed the Zone A document check, count and inspection are booked into the warehouse management system. Uncounted, uninspected, damaged or quarantined goods are never booked as available stock. Booking is the system confirmation that the stock in the system is the stock on the rack.

2. Booking is performed in Zone A immediately after release under PR-01, using the handheld WMS scanners. The inbound operator scans each released pallet and carton label, confirms client, product, quantity, batch or expiry date, and storage requirement. The booking records the inbound door from doors 1-4, delivery reference, time and operator identity.

3. No pallet is booked twice and no pallet leaves Zone A unbooked. Scanned quantities must match the checked delivery documents and the confirmed Zone A count. Any difference stops booking for that delivery, the pallets are held in the marked Zone A lanes, and the shift supervisor and dispatcher are informed before any put-away task is created.

4. Booking assigns every pallet its destination zone. Standard packed goods are assigned to Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions. Chilled goods are assigned to Zone E cold zone between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12. Hazmat is assigned only to the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F up to 4,000 kg under PR-13. Value-added, quarantine and returns areas in Zone F are never used as standard put-away destinations.

5. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Any pallet exceeding this weight, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label is not booked for put-away. It is segregated in Zone A, marked as pending, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day if damaged, under PR-09.

6. Only booked goods are released to put-away under PR-02. Release is a separate recorded step after booking: the inbound operator or shift supervisor confirms in the system that the booked pallets are free for collection to Zone B, E or F. Without this release, forklift operators do not move pallets out of Zone A.

7. Release creates a traceable put-away task for each pallet, with source location in Zone A and target zone and bay. Forklift operators execute only active scanner tasks with the electric fleet, observing the 8 km/h hall limit and the 5 km/h limit at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m are kept clear during collection.

8. Booked pallets are collected promptly so that Zone A is cleared for the next booked carrier at doors 1-4. Chilled pallets go to Zone E without delay to protect the cold chain, with manual temperature verification each shift. Hazmat pallets go directly to the Zone F cage and never wait in Zone B, C or D. Shortages, overages and quarantine transfers are noted on the release record.

9. Paperwork, scanner confirmations and release records are completed before the truck is released by the dispatcher and before the driver leaves the waiting area. Open bookings, unreleased pallets and pending discrepancies are not carried silently but are recorded by delivery and door for stock controller follow-up and incident review.

10. Every booking, release, delay and pending load is transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. At 14:00 and 22:00 the outgoing shift supervisor hands over which inbound loads are booked, which pallets are released and awaiting put-away to Zone B, E or F, and which deliveries are still held in Zone A, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Bulk storage in Zone B
text:
1. Zone B — bulk storage occupies 2,200 m2 and is the reserve store for the site. It holds only inspected and booked standard packed goods for replenishment of Zone C pick faces. Chilled goods are held in Zone E, hazmat only in the Zone F cage, and quarantine, returns and value-added work only in Zone F. No other goods are stored in Zone B.

2. High-bay pallet racking in Zone B provides 2,400 pallet positions. Every booked pallet has a single assigned rack position recorded in the warehouse management system. No pallet is placed in Zone B without an active put-away task under PR-02, and no position is double-occupied or used as a staging or overflow area for Zone A or Zone D.

3. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, including pallets and loads. This limit is fixed and applies to every bay regardless of position height or product type. The limit is built on the site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg. Overloading a bay is prohibited and is stopped immediately by the shift supervisor.

4. Pallets placed in racking must be stable, fully supported on the beams, without overhang, collapse or visible pallet damage. Any pallet exceeding 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label is not put away to Zone B. It is held in Zone A and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. Free block-stacking in Zone B outside the racking is permitted only in marked block areas and is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m stacking height. Stacks must be vertical, aligned and stable, on sound pallets of the same footprint. Damaged, leaning or mixed-footprint stacks are prohibited and are broken down immediately.

6. Main transport aisles through and around Zone B are 4.0 m wide and are kept fully clear at all times. Rack storage aisles between the high bays are 3.0 m wide and are kept clear of staged pallets, wrapping material and waste. No put-away, replenishment or counting task may block an aisle, a crossing or access to emergency equipment.

7. Pedestrian walkways bordering and crossing Zone B are 1.2 m wide, physically separated by yellow barriers. All movement on foot uses these walkways and marked crossings. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and ramp interfaces near Zone B.

8. High-bay work in Zone B is performed with the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t. General moves to and from the Zone B transfer lanes are performed with the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the electric pallet jacks and hand pallet jacks. Only authorised forklift operators drive trucks in Zone B, and trucks operate only on active scanner tasks.

9. Zone B discipline is enforced on every shift. Pallets are scanned to source and target locations, beam and bay labels are scan-verified, and empty or damaged positions are reported to the stock controllers. Reserve stock is not picked directly for customer orders; replenishment to Zone C takes place before each picking shift under PR-03.

10. Racking in Zone B is subject to documented safety inspection every month, with every repair logged by the maintenance technician. Any impact, deformation, loose beam, overload or falling material is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, the bay is blocked and unloaded if required, and the finding is carried into the end-of-shift handover under PR-15 until cleared.

title: Put-away process
text:
1. Put-away moves only goods that have been booked into the warehouse management system in Zone A under PR-01. Uncounted, uninspected, unbooked, damaged or quarantined goods are never put away. Forklift operators do not collect any pallet from Zone A without an active WMS scanner task created on release under PR-02.

2. Every put-away task links a booked pallet to a single destination location. Standard packed goods go to an assigned rack position or marked block area in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions. Chilled goods go to Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C. Hazmat goes only to the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F. No standard pallet is directed to Zone C, Zone D or the value-added, quarantine or returns areas.

3. Collection from Zone A is prompt and in task sequence. Forklift operators scan-verify the pallet label and source lane in Zone A before lifting, confirm the target zone and bay on the handheld scanner, and transport the pallet by the 4.0 m main transport aisles. Transport aisles, pedestrian walkways and the next inbound door lanes are kept clear during collection.

4. No pallet exceeding 800 kg including load, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label is put away. Such pallets are left in the marked Zone A lanes, reported to the shift supervisor, and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Beam labels and bay limits are never overridden to fit a non-conforming pallet.

5. Placement in Zone B high-bay racking is performed with the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, fed by the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and pallet jacks on the transfer lanes. The operator scan-verifies the bay and beam label before setting down, checks the pallet is fully supported without overhang, and confirms placement on the scanner. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg.

6. Free block-stacking outside the racking is used only in marked Zone B block areas and only where the task directs it. Stacks are limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m height, vertical and aligned on sound pallets of the same footprint. Leaning, mixed-footprint or damaged stacks are prohibited and are broken down and reported immediately.

7. Chilled put-away to Zone E is prioritised to protect the cold chain under PR-12. Chilled pallets are collected first, moved without delay or intermediate staging in Zone B, C or D, and confirmed in Zone E with temperature evidence intact. Any cold-chain deviation, alarm or damaged insulation is reported to the shift supervisor and the pallet is held for decision, not stored as available stock.

8. Hazmat put-away to the Zone F cage is direct and segregated under PR-13. Hazmat pallets are moved directly from Zone A to the cage, never staged in Zone B, C or D, and never together with food, drugstore or general goods on the same truck movement. Total storage in the cage never exceeds 4,000 kg, which is at most 5 full-weight pallets, and cage labelling and closure are checked on placement.

9. Only authorised forklift operators drive trucks on put-away, with seat belts fastened whenever the truck is moving. They observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramp interfaces, use only the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways on foot, and operate dock levellers only where trained. Trucks operate only after the documented check before first use each day under PR-10.

10. Every put-away is closed on the scanner with source, target, time and operator identity, and any exception is recorded for stock controller follow-up. Uncompleted tasks, blocked bays, overweight or damaged pallets and full locations are not carried silently but are reported to the shift supervisor and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, so Zone A is cleared and every booked pallet has a known owner.

title: Cold storage in Zone E
text:
1. Zone E — cold zone occupies 300 m2 and is the only chilled store on site. It holds only inspected and booked chilled packed goods that require storage between +2 °C and +8 °C. Standard ambient goods, hazmat, quarantine, returns and value-added work are never placed in Zone E, and chilled goods are never stored in Zone B, C, D or F.

2. The temperature in Zone E is held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times, including outside operating hours. Cooling equipment, doors, curtains and seals are kept closed and in serviceable condition to maintain the range. Doors are opened only for put-away, replenishment and counting tasks and are closed immediately afterwards.

3. Zone E is equipped with continuous temperature monitoring and alarms. Any alarm, deviation outside +2 °C to +8 °C, cooling fault, door fault or power interruption is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. Affected stock is held as not available, is not picked or replenished, and is not released until the cause is cleared and the temperature is verified back in range under PR-12.

4. A manual temperature verification is performed in Zone E on each shift. The morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 each record the reading, time, device and operator identity. Missing or failed verification stops chilled movements until a verified reading is recorded and reviewed by the shift supervisor.

5. Put-away to Zone E follows PR-02 and PR-12 and is prioritised. Chilled pallets are booked in Zone A under PR-01, released only after document check, count and inspection, and collected first for direct transfer to Zone E. There is no intermediate staging in Zone B, C or D, and no joint transport with hazmat or with damaged goods.

6. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Any chilled pallet exceeding this weight, unstable, overhanging, damaged, with broken cold-chain evidence, damaged insulation, or without a readable label and batch or expiry data is not stored as available stock. It is segregated, reported to the shift supervisor, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day if damaged under PR-09.

7. Storage inside Zone E uses only assigned, labelled chilled positions recorded in the warehouse management system. Every placement and removal is scan-verified by source and target on the handheld scanner. No position is double-occupied, and aisles, evaporators, sensors and emergency equipment are kept clear. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m with yellow barriers remain unobstructed.

8. Pick-face replenishment from Zone E to Zone C under PR-03 takes place before each picking shift and only against active scanner tasks. Chilled goods leave Zone E only for ordered replenishment, cycle counts or approved quarantine transfer. Exposure time outside the cold zone is kept to the minimum, and pallets not placed within the task are returned to Zone E without delay.

9. Only authorised forklift operators and trained inbound operators handle chilled moves, with seat belts fastened whenever the truck is moving. They observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramp interfaces. Trucks and pallet jacks used in Zone E must be clean, dry and free of contamination, and condensation and spillage are cleaned and reported immediately.

10. Every temperature reading, alarm, deviation, quarantine transfer and open chilled task is recorded for stock controller follow-up and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. At handover the outgoing shift supervisor confirms the last verified temperature, alarm status, stock held as unavailable, and pallets still awaiting put-away or replenishment, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Hazmat cage and quarantine in Zone F
text:
1. Zone F — services and control occupies 600 m2 and holds all non-standard stock functions. It contains value-added packing, quarantine, returns inspection and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. No standard ambient or chilled available stock is stored in Zone F, and no quarantine, returns or hazmat stock is held in Zone A, B, C, D or E.

2. The hazmat cage is the only permitted location for hazardous packed goods on site. Hazmat never sits anywhere else, not in receiving, bulk storage, picking, dispatch or the cold zone, and never in transit lanes, aisles or the yard. Every hazmat pallet recorded in the system has a cage location, and any pallet found outside the cage is stopped and reported immediately.

3. Total storage in the hazmat cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time. This limit is built on the site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg, which means at most 5 full-weight pallets in the cage. Before any put-away under PR-13 the forklift operator and shift supervisor confirm remaining capacity, and no task is created that would exceed the limit.

4. The cage is separate, ventilated, marked and lockable, with segregation, spill containment, fire and emergency equipment kept clear and serviceable. Access is limited to instructed staff under the shift supervisor. Labelling, closure, leakage checks and compatibility are verified on every placement and removal, and incompatible goods are never placed together.

5. Put-away to the cage follows PR-02 and PR-13 and is direct and segregated. Hazmat pallets are booked in Zone A only after document check, count and inspection, then moved directly from Zone A to the cage without staging in Zone B, C or D. Joint transport with food, drugstore, chilled or general goods on the same movement is prohibited.

6. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Any hazmat pallet exceeding this weight, unstable, overhanging, damaged, leaking, with broken seals, missing hazard labels or without a readable WMS label is not stored as available stock. It is segregated, the area is secured, and the shift supervisor initiates spill response and quarantine under PR-13 and PR-09.

7. Quarantine in Zone F holds all damaged, suspect and non-conforming goods pending decision under PR-09. Damaged goods go to quarantine the same day they are found, whether found in Zone A, B, C, D or E. Quarantined pallets are physically separated, clearly marked, system-blocked as not available, and are never picked, replenished, packed or dispatched.

8. Returns inspection takes place only in the marked returns area in Zone F under PR-07. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery, every unit is inspected, and only then is restock, rework or scrap proposed. Returns staff do not restock, rework or scrap without recorded approval of the final disposition by the shift supervisor, and approved restock goes only via booking to Zone B or E.

9. Every placement, removal and transfer in Zone F is scan-verified on the handheld WMS scanner by source and target, with time and operator identity. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack aisles of 3.0 m where applicable, and 1.2 m barrier-separated pedestrian walkways remain unobstructed. Trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps, with seat belts fastened whenever moving.

10. Cage stock, quarantine stock and open returns are recorded for stock controller follow-up and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit, quarantine quantities and causes, write-offs within the 500 EUR authority rule, and any spill, alarm or incident, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Picking zone layout
text:
1. Zone C — picking occupies 1,200 m2 and is the only zone where customer orders are picked. No picking takes place in Zone B, E, F, A or D, and no reserve, quarantine, hazmat or staged outbound stock is held in Zone C. All ten pickers work in Zone C against active WMS scanner tasks under PR-04.

2. Zone C holds ground-level pick faces fed from bulk storage. Each pick face has a single fixed location recorded in the warehouse management system, with a readable location label, product identity, and batch or expiry data where applicable. A face holds only one product at a time and only in quantities for order picking, never as reserve storage.

3. Part of the pick faces are configured as flow racks with roller lanes loaded from the rear and picked from the front. Rear loading lanes are served by forklift operators on replenishment tasks, front picking aisles are served on foot by pickers. First-in, first-out rotation is maintained by lane discipline, and no pallet or carton is placed outside its lane.

4. The layout separates replenishment flows from picking flows. Rear supply aisles connect Zone C to Zone B bulk storage and to Zone E for chilled faces, and are used only by authorised forklift operators with pallet jacks, electric pallet jacks and counterbalance trucks. Front picking aisles are used on foot with hand pallet jacks and picking carts, using the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways and marked crossings.

5. Standard ambient faces are fed exclusively from Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions under PR-03. Chilled pick faces, where assigned, are fed exclusively from Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12, with minimum exposure time outside the cold zone. Hazmat, quarantine and returns stock are never placed on pick faces.

6. Reserve stock is never picked directly. Bulk pallets stay in Zone B or Zone E until released as a replenishment task, and only the released quantity is brought to the assigned face or flow-rack lane. Overfilling of faces, double occupation, and staging of reserve pallets in picking aisles are prohibited.

7. Before each picking shift the pick faces are replenished to the defined fill level so that picking starts with full availability. Open replenishment from the previous shift is completed first, empty lanes and zero-stock faces are reported to the stock controllers, and no picking task is started on a face flagged as empty or blocked.

8. Every face and lane is scan-controlled. Replenishment placement is scan-verified by source and target on the handheld WMS scanners, of which the teams share 20, and picking is scan-verified item by item before packing. Damaged, mislabelled or unreadable labels, unstable pallets and any pallet, load included, above 800 kg are not placed on faces and are reported to the shift supervisor.

9. Main transport aisles around Zone C are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, kept fully clear of pallets, film, cardboard and waste. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and interfaces to Zone C. Pedestrians use only the walkways and crossings and have priority.

10. Zone C is cleared and ordered by task. Packaging waste is removed to the cardboard baler, spillages and condensation are cleaned and reported immediately, and blocked faces, damaged racking and missing labels are logged for the maintenance technician and stock controllers. Open faces, pending replenishment and faults are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

title: Replenishment of pick faces
text:
1. Replenishment of pick faces is performed under PR-03 and takes place before each picking shift. No picking shift starts with unfilled faces. The morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 each begin only after the assigned faces in Zone C have been checked, filled to the defined fill level, and released for picking.

2. Only reserve stock from bulk storage is used for replenishment. Standard ambient faces are fed exclusively from Zone B with 2,400 pallet positions. Chilled faces, where assigned, are fed exclusively from Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12. No face is filled from Zone A, Zone D, quarantine, returns or the hazmat cage.

3. Replenishment runs only against active WMS scanner tasks. The stock controllers or the shift supervisor release the tasks by face, product and quantity on the basis of system stock and open orders. Forklift operators do not bring reserve pallets to Zone C without a task, and pickers do not pick directly from reserve stock in Zone B or Zone E.

4. Open replenishment from the previous shift is completed first. Pallets still in transfer lanes, half-filled flow-rack lanes and faces flagged as empty or blocked are cleared, placed or reported before new tasks start. Empty lanes and zero-stock faces are reported to the stock controllers for adjustment review with a second count before any correction.

5. Execution is by authorised forklift operators only, using the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and electric pallet jacks. The operator scans the source location in Zone B or Zone E, scans the pallet label, transports by the 4.0 m main transport aisles, and scans the target face or rear loading lane in Zone C on the handheld WMS scanners.

6. Flow racks are loaded only from the rear supply aisles and picked only from the front. The operator places cartons or replenishment units into the assigned roller lane without overfilling, maintains first-in, first-out order, and confirms placement on the scanner. No pallet, carton or unit is placed outside its lane, on the floor of the picking aisle, or on another product face.

7. Quantity discipline applies to every face. Only the tasked quantity is brought forward, and faces are never overfilled, double-occupied or used as reserve storage. Bulk pallets that are not fully consumed by the task remain in Zone B or Zone E on their recorded location. Staging of reserve pallets in Zone C picking aisles, front aisles and crossings is prohibited.

8. No non-conforming pallet is placed on a pick face. A pallet, load included, of more than 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged, mislabelled or without a readable label is not replenished. Chilled units with broken cold-chain evidence or damaged insulation are not replenished. Such stock is segregated, reported to the shift supervisor, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day if damaged under PR-09.

9. Replenishment observes all movement and safety rules. Trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and Zone C interfaces. Seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving. Front picking aisles remain free for pickers on foot using the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and rear aisles of 3.0 m are kept clear during lane loading.

10. Every replenishment is closed on the scanner with source, target, quantity, time and operator identity, and exceptions are recorded for stock controller follow-up. Uncompleted faces, blocked lanes, missing labels and rack damage are reported to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. Open faces, pending tasks and chilled exposure issues are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

title: Order picking with scanners
text:
1. Order picking is performed only in Zone C and only against active WMS scanner tasks under PR-04. No picking takes place in Zone A, B, D, E or F, and no picker picks from reserve stock, quarantine, returns or the hazmat cage. A task is started only after the assigned pick faces have been replenished and released for the shift.

2. The ten pickers work in Zone C on ground-level pick faces and flow-rack front aisles, using the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners. Each picker logs on with personal identity, accepts one task at a time, and follows the scanner sequence by location, product, quantity and batch or expiry where applicable. Tasks are never split, reordered or shared without instruction from the shift supervisor.

3. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. The picker scans the face or lane label, then scans each item or carton label, and confirms quantity on the scanner. The system blocks mismatched product, wrong batch, over-pick and short-pick. Unverified, unscanned or manually counted items are never forwarded to packing or Zone D.

4. First-in, first-out rotation is mandatory. Flow racks are picked only from the front picking side in lane order, and ground faces are picked from the indicated stock. Where batch or expiry is directed by the scanner, only that batch is picked. Expired, damaged, mislabelled or unreadable stock is not picked but segregated, reported to the shift supervisor, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. Pick faces are never over-picked or forcibly emptied. If the tasked quantity is not fully available, the face is empty, the label is missing, or the scanner flags zero stock, picking for that line stops. The picker records the short pick on the scanner, leaves the lane clear, and informs the shift supervisor and stock controllers for second count and replenishment review.

6. Picked goods are placed only in designated picking carts, totes or pallets for that order, by order and line. Mixed orders, mixed batches and loose stacking are prohibited. Stability, weight distribution and the site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg are observed. Unstable, overhanging or damaged units are not built into outbound pallets.

7. Cleanliness and order are maintained during picking. Packaging waste, film and cardboard are removed from picking aisles to the cardboard baler, spillages and condensation are cleaned and reported immediately, and front picking aisles, crossings and the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways are kept clear. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m are never blocked with picked stock.

8. Movement discipline in Zone C separates pickers on foot from replenishment trucks. Pickers use only walkways and marked crossings on foot, with high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet. Pickers make eye contact before crossing and never step into rear supply aisles during lane loading.

9. Completed picks are closed line by line on the scanner with location, quantity, time and picker identity, then handed for packing, labelling and transfer to Zone D under PR-05. Only scan-verified, fully confirmed picks leave Zone C. Partial picks, pending lines and quarantine findings stay under control in Zone C until resolved or re-tasked by the shift supervisor.

10. Every completed task, short pick, blocked face, label fault and damage is recorded for stock controller follow-up and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms open orders, pending replenishment to Zone C, and faces flagged empty or blocked, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Packing and labelling
text:
1. Packing and labelling is performed under PR-05 and covers all picked goods after scan-verified picking in Zone C. No picked item moves to Zone D without verification, correct packing, correct labelling and wrapping. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D in front of outbound docks 5-8.

2. Only scan-verified picks leave Zone C for packing. Packing staff accept only lines closed on the handheld WMS scanners with location, quantity, time and picker identity. Unscanned, partially picked or manually counted goods are refused, held in Zone C and reported to the shift supervisor.

3. Packing is done by order and line in the designated packing areas and in value-added packing in Zone F. Goods are packed by client, order and delivery, with batch or expiry separation where directed. Mixed orders, mixed batches and loose stacking are prohibited. Stability and weight distribution are checked on every pallet.

4. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Overweight, unstable, overhanging or damaged pallets are not packed for dispatch. Such pallets are segregated, reported to the shift supervisor and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. Every outbound pallet and carton carries a readable system label before transfer to Zone D. Labels are printed and checked against the WMS scanner task for client, product, quantity, destination and outbound door. Mislabelled, unreadable or missing labels stop the pallet, which is held for correction and re-verification.

6. Wrapping is performed on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers operated only by instructed packing and forklift staff. Pallets are wrapped to a stable, transport-safe standard with base and top coverage, without crushing cartons or obscuring labels. Unstable wraps are re-wrapped, and film waste is removed immediately.

7. Packaging waste is handled continuously. Cardboard, cartons and damaged packaging are removed from packing areas to the 1 cardboard baler, which is operated only by instructed staff. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack aisles of 3.0 m and the 1.2 m barrier-separated pedestrian walkways are kept clear of pallets, film and waste at all times.

8. Damaged, expired or suspect goods found during packing are not packed, labelled or wrapped. They are segregated, marked, system-blocked where required and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The finding is recorded for stock controller follow-up and incident review by the shift supervisor.

9. All packing work follows movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, seat belts are fastened whenever a truck is moving, and limits of 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are observed. Pedestrians use only walkways and marked crossings.

10. Every packed, labelled and wrapped pallet is confirmed on the scanner with order, pallet identity, time and operator identity, and handed for staging to Zone D under PR-06. Open orders, pending labels, re-wraps and quarantine transfers are reported to the shift supervisor and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

title: Dispatch staging in Zone D
text:
1. Zone D — dispatch occupies 900 m2 in front of outbound docks 5-8 and is the only outbound staging area on site. It holds only packed, labelled and wrapped pallets that have been confirmed under PR-05 and assigned to a specific outbound door and load. No unwrapped, unlabelled, unpacked or scan-unconfirmed goods are held in Zone D.

2. Staging in Zone D follows PR-06 Outbound dispatch and runs only against an active outbound task. Packing staff and forklift operators move pallets to Zone D only after scanner confirmation of order, pallet identity, time and operator identity. Pallets without a readable system label for client, product, quantity, destination and door are refused and held for correction.

3. Every pallet in Zone D is staged by door, load and time slot. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door from doors 5-8 and a fixed time slot, and defines the staging sequence per shift. No pallet is staged for an unbooked truck, and no inbound work, quarantine, returns or hazmat stock is staged in Zone D.

4. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Any pallet exceeding this weight, unstable, overhanging, damaged, with a broken wrap or obscured label is not staged for dispatch. It is segregated within Zone D, reported to the shift supervisor, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day if damaged under PR-09.

5. Zone D lanes, door aprons and markings are kept strictly separated. Staged pallets are placed only in the marked door lanes for doors 5-8, aligned and stable, without blocking neighbouring doors, levellers, emergency equipment or sensors. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m where applicable are kept fully clear at all times.

6. Handling in Zone D is performed only by authorised forklift operators with the electric fleet and by packing staff with hand pallet jacks. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and electric pallet jacks perform staging moves, and the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers are used only for re-wrap where instructed. Seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving.

7. Movement and pedestrian discipline applies throughout staging. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Pedestrians use only the 1.2 m walkways physically separated by yellow barriers and marked crossings, and have priority. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory.

8. Drivers do not take part in staging and do not enter Zone D or the hall. They wait only in the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard until called to their assigned door. Each dock door is at 1.2 m dock height with its own leveller, operated only by trained warehouse staff. Dock doors 5-8 are outbound only and are kept closed until the truck is docked and the dispatcher releases the load.

9. Staged loads remain under the control of the dispatcher and shift supervisor until release. Short picks, missing pallets, label faults and damaged wraps are reported immediately, corrected before loading, and recorded for stock controller follow-up. No staged pallet leaves Zone D, and no truck is loaded or sealed, without dispatcher release under PR-06.

10. Zone D is cleared by load so that the next booked carrier can dock. Completed stages, open loads, trucks in the waiting area and rebooked slots are recorded by door and delivery and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. At handover the outgoing shift supervisor confirms which doors are staged, which loads are released and awaiting loading, and which pallets are still pending, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Load release and truck loading
text:
1. No outbound truck is loaded without prior dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Release is a separate recorded step after staging in Zone D and confirms that the load is complete, that every pallet is wrapped, labelled and scanner-confirmed, and that the assigned carrier, door from doors 5-8 and time slot match the booking.

2. The dispatcher owns release and dock sequencing for the whole site. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot, calls the truck from the marked waiting area in the fenced yard only when Zone D and the door are ready, and defines the loading order by load and delivery. No truck moves to a door without dispatcher instruction.

3. Drivers wait only in the marked waiting area until called and never enter the hall or Zone D. On call, the driver reverses to the assigned outbound door, secures the vehicle, switches off the engine where required, and returns to the waiting area or the defined cab interface. Drivers do not take part in staging, loading, wrapping or sealing.

4. Each outbound dock is at 1.2 m dock height and has its own leveller. The leveller is operated only by trained warehouse staff, never by the driver. The door is kept closed until the truck is correctly docked, the vehicle is secured, and the dispatcher has released the load. Pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are limited to 5 km/h.

5. Only pallets staged in the marked door lanes for doors 5-8 are loaded. Loading is performed only by authorised forklift operators with the electric fleet and by packing staff in support, using the handheld WMS scanners. Every pallet is scan-verified against the release before it leaves Zone D, and pallets without a readable system label are refused.

6. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. No overweight, unstable, overhanging, damaged, unwrapped or mislabelled pallet is loaded. Broken wraps, obscured labels and damage found during loading stop loading for that pallet, which is segregated in Zone D, reported to the shift supervisor and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

7. Loading follows the release sequence by door, load and delivery, with weight distribution, stability and transport safety observed on every trailer. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m are kept clear, the hall limit of 8 km/h is observed, seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving, and high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor.

8. After loading is complete, the count is reconciled pallet by pallet against the release and the transport documents. Shortages, overages and refused pallets are recorded, reported to the dispatcher and shift supervisor, and held in Zone D for correction. An incomplete or disputed load is not sealed and does not leave until the discrepancy is resolved and re-released.

9. Sealing is performed only after reconciliation and only on dispatcher instruction. The outbound operators close, seal and record the seal number against the delivery, door, carrier and time. The documents are handed over at the door interface, the driver confirms receipt, and the dispatcher records departure. No sealed truck is reopened without dispatcher and shift supervisor approval.

10. Every release, loading, sealing, delay and open load is recorded by door and delivery and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms which loads are released and loaded, which trucks are still in the waiting area, which doors are staged for the next shift, and which discrepancies remain, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Pallet weight and trailer capacity
text:
1. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. This is the fixed site standard on which every storage, handling and transport capacity is built. No pallet exceeding 800 kg is packed, booked, staged or loaded, and no calculation, bay limit or load plan assumes a higher pallet weight.

2. The standard applies to the complete unit: pallet, goods, packaging, film and label combined. Packed, labelled and wrapped pallets are checked for stability, weight distribution and readable labelling before they leave packing. Overweight, unstable, overhanging or damaged pallets are segregated and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

3. Outbound transport by trailer uses contracted curtain-side trailers rated at 22,000 kg payload on 33 floor positions. Both figures apply together: the trailer is limited by total weight to 22,000 kg and by floor space to 33 pallet positions. Neither limit may be exceeded on any load released under PR-06.

4. The maximum number of full-weight pallets per trailer follows directly from these two limits. By weight: 22,000 kg divided by 800 kg per pallet equals 27.5 pallets, so at most 27 full-weight pallets. By floor space: 33 positions would allow 33 pallets. The lower of the two results governs, so a trailer takes at most 27 full-weight pallets.

5. In practice the weight limit governs all full-weight loads and the floor limit governs only light loads. Twenty-seven pallets of 800 kg reach 21,600 kg on 27 of the 33 positions, leaving 6 positions empty by weight. Thirty-three pallets can only be loaded together if their combined weight stays within 22,000 kg, which requires an average of no more than 666 kg per pallet.

6. Loading plans are built from the WMS scanner data by pallet identity and weight. The dispatcher and shift supervisor confirm before release that the sum of pallet weights for the trailer does not exceed 22,000 kg and that the number of pallets does not exceed 33 positions. A planned load exceeding either figure is split across two trailers before staging in Zone D.

7. Weight distribution, stability and transport safety are observed on every trailer in addition to the totals. Heavy pallets are placed to keep axle loads within the trailer rating, stable and fully wrapped units only are loaded, and base and top wrap coverage is checked at the door. Unstable wraps are re-wrapped on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers before loading.

8. No overweight pallet is compensated by leaving another position empty. Because the 800 kg pallet limit protects rack bays at 2,700 kg, reach trucks at 1.6 t, counterbalance trucks at 2.5 t and manual handling, any pallet above 800 kg is refused for dispatch even if the trailer total would remain below 22,000 kg. It is segregated in Zone D and reported to the shift supervisor.

9. Every trailer load is reconciled pallet by pallet at loading against the dispatcher release. The count records pallet identities, individual weights where directed, total weight against the 22,000 kg limit, positions used against the 33 positions, door from doors 5-8, carrier and time. Shortages, overages and refused pallets stop sealing until the load is corrected and re-released.

10. Planned trailer totals, actual totals and any split loads are recorded by door and delivery and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms which trailers were completed within the 27-pallet and 22,000 kg limits, which loads were split, and which pallets remain staged in Zone D, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Van and shift dispatch limit
text:
1. Outbound transport by van uses the site delivery van rated at 1,200 kg payload on 6 floor positions. Both figures apply together: the van is limited by total weight to 1,200 kg and by floor space to 6 pallet positions. Neither limit may be exceeded on any load released under PR-06.

2. The maximum number of full-weight pallets per van follows directly from these two limits. By weight: 1,200 kg divided by 800 kg per pallet equals 1 pallet with 400 kg reserve. By floor space: 6 positions would allow 6 pallets. The lower of the two results governs, so the van takes at most one full-weight pallet.

3. In practice the weight limit always governs full-weight loads and the floor limit governs only light loads. One pallet of 800 kg uses 800 kg of the van limit on 1 of the 6 positions, leaving 400 kg reserve and 5 positions unusable by weight for full-weight pallets. Six pallets can only be loaded together if their combined weight stays within 1,200 kg, which requires an average of no more than 200 kg per pallet.

4. The allocation rule is fixed: the van carries single-pallet and small consignments up to 1,200 kg total. One full-weight pallet goes by van, and anything heavier goes by trailer. Two full-weight pallets, any load above 1,200 kg total, and any pallet build that would exceed van stability or wrap safety is planned as a trailer load from the start.

5. No overweight pallet is compensated on the van by leaving positions empty. Because the 800 kg pallet limit protects rack bays, trucks and handling, any pallet above 800 kg is refused for dispatch even if the van total would remain below 1,200 kg. It is segregated in Zone D, reported to the shift supervisor and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

6. Outbound door capacity is fixed by doors and turnaround. Four outbound doors are available, doors 5-8 outbound only, each handling 3 trailer loads per shift. No inbound work takes place at these doors, and no truck is loaded without dispatcher assignment of door and time slot and without dispatcher release under PR-06.

7. The maximum dispatch promise per shift follows directly from door capacity and trailer capacity. Four doors multiplied by 3 trailer loads per door equals 12 trailer loads per shift. Twelve loads multiplied by 27 full-weight pallets per trailer equals 324 full-weight pallets per shift. This is the most that can be promised to a client for one shift.

8. The 324-pallet figure is a promise limit, not a staging target. The dispatcher and shift supervisor confirm before release that the sum of booked pallets for the shift does not exceed 324 full-weight equivalents and that door sequencing, Zone D staging of 900 m2, stretch-wrapper output and scanner-confirmed labour cover the plan. A plan exceeding the limit is split across shifts before staging.

9. Van loads are handled within the same doors, staging and release discipline but do not increase the 324-pallet promise. Vans are assigned to doors 5-8 by the dispatcher, staged only as wrapped, labelled and scanner-confirmed pallets in marked door lanes in Zone D, and scan-verified pallet by pallet at loading. Weight distribution, stability and the 1.2 m door leveller procedure apply equally to vans and trailers.

10. Every van load and every trailer slot is reconciled by door, delivery, pallet identities, total weight against the 1,200 kg or 22,000 kg limit, and positions used against the 6 or 33 positions. Planned totals, actual totals, split loads and rebooked slots are recorded and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for completed, loaded and still-staged pallets.

title: Hazmat cage pallet limit
text:
1. Total storage in the ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time. This is a fixed safety limit that applies to all hazardous packed goods together, including pallets, goods, packaging and containment combined. No put-away, replenishment or returns transfer may create or increase stock beyond this total.

2. The cage limit is built on the same site standard as all other capacities: a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg. No hazmat pallet exceeding 800 kg is booked, put away or stored, and no calculation for the cage assumes a higher pallet weight. Overweight, unstable, leaking or mislabelled pallets are refused and handled under PR-13 and PR-09.

3. The maximum number of full-weight pallets in the cage follows directly from these two figures. By weight: 4,000 kg divided by 800 kg per pallet equals 5 pallets. The cage of 60 m2 would physically allow more floor positions, but floor space does not govern. The weight limit governs, so the cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets.

4. In practice this means the cage fills by weight long before it fills by floor area. Five pallets of 800 kg reach exactly 4,000 kg and close the cage to any further receipt, even if marked positions stand empty. More than 5 pallets can only be held together if their combined weight stays within 4,000 kg, which requires a correspondingly lower average weight per pallet.

5. Capacity is checked before every task is created. The forklift operator and the shift supervisor confirm the current cage weight in the warehouse management system, add the planned inbound weight, and confirm remaining capacity. No put-away task under PR-02 and PR-13 is released from Zone A if the addition would exceed 4,000 kg.

6. No compensation by stacking, double occupation or temporary staging is permitted. Because the 4,000 kg limit protects ventilation, segregation, spill containment and emergency access in the 60 m2 cage, an excess pallet is never squeezed in, never stored in the aisles around the cage, and never staged in Zone A, B, C, D or E. Excess receipts are held in Zone A for refusal or rebooking.

7. The cage remains the only permitted location for hazmat on site. Hazmat never sits in receiving, bulk storage with 2,400 positions, picking, dispatch or the cold zone, and never in transit lanes, on dock aprons or in the yard. Every hazmat pallet in the system carries a cage location, and any pallet found outside the cage stops work until secured.

8. Placement and removal are scan-verified by source and target on the handheld WMS scanners, with labelling, closure, leakage checks and compatibility confirmed on each movement. Incompatible goods are never placed together to use weight reserve. Spill equipment, fire equipment and ventilation are kept clear, and any leak, damaged seal or missing hazard label blocks the movement and triggers spill response.

9. Every cage movement is reconciled against the limit at placement. The record shows pallet identities, individual weights, total cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit, pallets on hand against the 5-pallet full-weight equivalent, door reference from doors 1-4, time and operator identity. Shortages, refusals and quarantine transfers to quarantine in Zone F are recorded and reviewed by the shift supervisor.

10. Planned totals, actual totals, refused receipts and remaining capacity are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms the current cage weight, number of pallets on hand, stock held as unavailable, write-offs within the 500 EUR authority rule, and any alarm, spill or incident, with clear ownership for the incoming shift and no silent carry-over.

title: Daily cycle counts
text:
1. Cycle counts run every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule. Counting never stops: each working day a defined part of Zone B bulk storage, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone and Zone F cage and quarantine is counted, so that all locations are covered in rotation. No working day passes without a released count task.

2. The two stock controllers own daily cycle counts under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts.
