They define the daily rotation, release count tasks on the handheld WMS scanners, direct second counts and recounts, investigate discrepancies, and prepare adjustments. The shift supervisor on duty ensures labour, scanners and access, and stops picking, replenishment or put-away in the counted lanes until the count is closed.

3. Counting runs only against active WMS scanner tasks. The stock controller assigns locations by zone, bay, face or cage position, with product, batch or expiry where applicable. Counters scan the location label, then scan each pallet and carton label, and confirm quantity on the scanner. Manual estimates, unscaned quantities and counts from memory are prohibited.

4. Counts are performed without interrupting zone discipline. Only inspected and booked stock is counted as available; quarantine in Zone F, returns pending inspection, hazmat in the 60 m2 cage and any pallet held in Zone A awaiting booking are counted separately as blocked or unavailable. A pallet, load included, of more than 800 kg, unstable or without a readable label is reported, not counted as conforming stock.

5. Zone B counts cover the 2,400 high-bay positions and marked block areas limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. The counter verifies pallet presence, beam and bay labels, and the 2,700 kg bay limit evidence. Zone C counts cover ground-level faces and flow-rack lanes by product and lane, with first-in, first-out order and single-product occupation verified. Empty faces and zero-stock flags are confirmed on the scanner.

6. Zone E counts are performed with minimum exposure time and doors closed immediately afterwards. The +2 °C to +8 °C range, last manual verification of the shift and alarm status are checked before chilled counting starts. Zone F counts cover the hazmat cage against the 4,000 kg limit, quarantine quantities and returns inspection stock separately. Cold-chain evidence and hazard labelling are verified during the count.

7. The system stock is the stock on the rack: every count is reconciled immediately against the warehouse management system. Matches are closed on the scanner with location, quantity, time and counter identity. Any difference stops closure for that location, the location is physically secured and marked for recount, and the shift supervisor and stock controllers are informed before any further movement.

8. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. A different counter from the first count recounts the secured location independently, re-scans all labels and confirms batch, expiry and unit of measure. Only if the second count confirms the difference does the stock controller prepare an adjustment with cause, quantity and value. Unconfirmed differences are recounted again until resolved.

9. Adjustments from cycle counts are documented by location, delivery reference where traceable, and counter identities for both counts. Damaged goods found during counting go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Racking damage, loose beams, overload or falling material found during counting is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and the bay is blocked.

10. Every daily count, second count, pending recount and prepared adjustment is recorded for follow-up and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms which zones were counted, which locations are blocked for recount, which adjustments await approval, and which quarantine transfers remain open, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Annual wall-to-wall stocktake
text:
1. Once a year the site shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. All receiving at doors 1-4, put-away, replenishment, picking in Zone C, packing and dispatch at doors 5-8 are stopped for the stocktake period. No handling, loading or movement takes place except on stocktake instruction.

2. The stocktake covers every stocked location on site in one continuous count. Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 high-bay positions and marked block areas, all Zone C pick faces and flow-rack lanes, Zone E cold zone, the 60 m2 hazmat cage in Zone F, quarantine, returns inspection stock and any booked pallets held in Zone A or Zone D are all counted. No location is excluded or carried forward from cycle counts.

3. The two stock controllers prepare and lead the stocktake. They freeze system stock, define the count sequence by zone, bay, face and cage position, release count tasks on the 20 handheld WMS scanners, assign independent count teams, and control recounts and adjustment preparation. The shift supervisors secure zones, provide labour and scanners, and enforce the shutdown.

4. Counting runs only against active stocktake scanner tasks with personal identity. Each team scans the location label, then scans every pallet and carton label, and confirms quantity, product, batch or expiry where applicable. Manual estimates, unscanned quantities and counts from memory are prohibited. A pallet, load included, of more than 800 kg, unstable or without a readable label is reported separately.

5. Zone discipline is maintained throughout the shutdown. Only inspected and booked stock is counted as available; quarantine in Zone F, returns pending inspection, damaged goods and hazmat stock are counted separately as blocked. Zone E is counted with minimum exposure time and doors closed immediately afterwards within +2 °C to +8 °C. The cage is reconciled against the 4,000 kg limit, at most 5 full-weight pallets.

6. Every location is reconciled immediately against the warehouse management system: the stock in the system must be the stock on the rack. Matches are closed on the scanner with location, quantity, time and counter identity. Any difference stops closure for that location, the location is physically secured and marked, and no goods move there until the recount is complete.

7. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. A different team from the first count recounts the secured location independently, re-scans all labels and confirms unit of measure, batch and expiry. Only a confirmed difference is prepared as an adjustment with cause, quantity, value and both counter identities. Unconfirmed differences are recounted again until resolved.

8. Damaged, expired or suspect goods found during the stocktake go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Racking damage, loose beams, evidence of breach of the 2,700 kg bay limit or the 3-high and 4.0 m block limit is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and the bay is blocked and logged.

9. The stocktake result becomes binding only with the signature of the warehouse manager. The stock controllers present full counts, second counts, recounts and prepared adjustments by zone and value, and the warehouse manager signs off the results. No stocktake is closed, no adjustment is posted to the system, and no write-off above 500 EUR is approved without this sign-off.

10. All counts, recounts, adjustments, quarantine transfers and remaining blocks are recorded by location and handed over in the documented record under PR-15. After sign-off the system is unfrozen, zones are released in sequence for replenishment and dispatch, and any open blocks, quarantine stock and follow-up counts are transferred to the shift supervisors with clear ownership for the next working shift.

title: Racking care and stock accuracy
text:
1. The stock in the system is the stock on the rack. Every pallet in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, in Zone C pick faces, in Zone E cold zone and in the Zone F cage and quarantine has one recorded location in the warehouse management system. No pallet exists on the floor without a system location, and no system location exists without a physical pallet.

2. The two stock controllers own stock accuracy day to day under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. They run daily cycle counts on the rotating zone schedule, direct second counts and recounts, investigate every difference, and prepare adjustments. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count by a different counter, with both identities recorded.

3. High-bay racking in Zone B is used only within its fixed limits. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg including pallets and loads, built on the site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg. No bay is overloaded, double-occupied or used for staging, and beam and bay labels are scan-verified on every put-away, replenishment and count.

4. Only conforming pallets are placed in racking. Pallets must be stable, fully supported on the beams, without overhang, collapse or visible pallet damage, with a readable label. Any pallet exceeding 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged or unreadable is not stored in racking, is segregated, and if damaged is moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. Free block-stacking outside the racking is permitted only in marked Zone B block areas and is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m stacking height. Stacks must be vertical, aligned and stable on sound pallets of the same footprint. Leaning, mixed-footprint, damaged or overheight stacks are prohibited and are broken down immediately and reported.

6. Racking is subject to documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects uprights, beams, fixings, beam locks, bracing and floor fixings across Zone B, Zone C flow racks and Zone E positions, and records the result with date, area and signature. Every repair is logged, and faults affecting load capacity block the bay until cleared.

7. Any impact, deformation, loose beam, cracked upright, overload evidence or falling material is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. The bay or lane is blocked, unloaded if required, and secured against put-away, replenishment and picking. The finding is treated as an incident, reviewed by the shift supervisor, and passed to the maintenance technician for logging.

8. Aisles, sensors and safety equipment around racking are kept clear at all times. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m, and 1.2 m barrier-separated pedestrian walkways with yellow barriers are never blocked with pallets, film or waste. High-bay work is by authorised forklift operators only, with the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and 6 counterbalance trucks rated at 2.5 t, at 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings.

9. Damaged, expired or suspect goods found on racking or during counts go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. They are physically separated, marked, system-blocked as not available, and never picked, replenished or dispatched. Write-offs follow the 500 EUR authority rule, with the shift supervisor approving up to 500 EUR and the warehouse manager approving above 500 EUR.

10. Every racking inspection, repair, blocked bay, quarantine transfer, second count and prepared adjustment is recorded for follow-up and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms bays blocked, cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit, Zone E temperature status, and locations awaiting recount, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Returns acceptance and inspection
text:
1. Returns are accepted only in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling and only within 14 days of delivery. The 14-day count runs from the documented delivery date to the date the goods physically arrive back on site. Returns arriving after 14 days are refused, held segregated, and reported to the shift supervisor and dispatcher for client clarification.

2. All returns arrive on the basis of prior booking by the dispatcher. Every return carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot, reports to the yard entrance, and waits in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard until called. Drivers never enter the hall or Zone F and take no part in unloading, inspection or decision.

3. Unloading of returns takes place only at the assigned door from doors 1-4, by trained inbound and returns staff with pallet jacks and the electric fleet. The dock leveller at the 1.2 m door is operated only by trained warehouse staff. Unloaded return pallets remain under control in Zone A reception lanes only for transfer and are moved promptly to the marked returns inspection area in Zone F.

4. No returned goods are restocked, reworked, repacked or dispatched on arrival. Every return is system-blocked as not available on receipt in the warehouse management system, using the handheld WMS scanners. Blocked returns are never placed on pick faces in Zone C, in Zone B bulk storage, in Zone E, or in Zone D staging.

5. Inspection takes place only in the marked returns area in Zone F and only by the four returns and packing staff. Returns staff work under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty and follow PR-07 step by step. Inspection does not start until the delivery reference, client, original delivery date, quantity and reason for return are recorded by return and pallet.

6. Every returned unit is inspected individually, without sampling. Packaging integrity, sealing, labelling, batch and expiry data, temperature evidence for chilled goods, hazard labelling and closure for hazmat, contamination, damage and signs of use or tampering are checked and recorded. Uninspected, unscanned or manually estimated units are never forwarded for decision.

7. Chilled returns are moved to Zone F without delay and with minimum exposure time outside +2 °C to +8 °C under PR-12. Hazmat returns are moved directly to the segregated returns area and then to the 60 m2 ventilated cage procedure under PR-13, never staged in Zone B, C, D or E. Any leak, damage, alarm or cold-chain deviation is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the area is secured.

8. Damaged, expired, suspect or non-conforming units found during inspection go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09. They are physically separated, clearly marked, system-blocked as not available, and are never picked, replenished, packed or dispatched. The finding, quantity, cause and source return are recorded for incident review.

9. All inspection work follows movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways with yellow barriers are kept clear.

10. Every receipt, inspection result, quarantine transfer and pending decision is recorded with time and operator identity and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms which returns arrived, which units are inspected and awaiting disposition approval, which pallets are in quarantine, and cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Restock, rework or scrap decisions
text:
1. No returned unit is restocked, reworked or scrapped without a recorded disposition decision. Inspection alone under PR-07 does not release goods. Every unit inspected in the marked returns area in Zone F stays system-blocked as not available until its disposition is approved and posted.

2. The four returns and packing staff propose the disposition for every inspected unit: restock to available stock, rework in value-added packing, or scrap. The proposal is recorded by return, pallet, product, quantity, batch or expiry, reason for return and inspection finding, with time and operator identity on the handheld WMS scanners.

3. Only units in original, intact, clean, correctly labelled and in-date condition with full traceability are proposed for restock. Chilled units are proposed for restock only with intact cold-chain evidence within +2 °C to +8 °C under PR-12. Hazmat units are proposed for restock only with intact closure, seals and hazard labels under PR-13.

4. Units with damaged packaging, missing labels, broken seals, repairable contamination of outer packaging or correctable labelling faults are proposed for rework. Rework takes place only in value-added packing in Zone F on instruction, with repacking, relabelling and re-inspection. Reworked units return for second inspection before any restock.

5. Units that are damaged, expired, used, tampered, contaminated, without cold-chain evidence, leaking, or otherwise non-conforming and not reworkable are proposed for scrap. Proposed scrap is moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day, physically separated, clearly marked and system-blocked, and is never picked, packed or dispatched.

6. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of all inspected returns. No restock, rework or scrap takes place without this recorded approval. The supervisor checks the inspection record, cold-chain and hazmat evidence, and quarantine transfers, and confirms or amends the proposal under PR-07 and PR-09.

7. Approved restock is booked back to available stock only via the warehouse management system. Standard goods go to an assigned location in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, chilled goods to Zone E, hazmat to the 60 m2 ventilated cage subject to the 4,000 kg limit. Pick faces in Zone C and staging in Zone D are never used as direct restock destinations.

8. Write-off authority for scrap and damaged goods follows the fixed 500 EUR threshold. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case. Any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold, and every write-off records cause, quantity, value and disposition.

9. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg on restock, rework or scrap movement. Overweight, unstable, overhanging or unreadable pallets are not restocked. Scrap pallets are secured for disposal, film and cardboard waste is removed to the 1 cardboard baler, and main transport aisles of 4.0 m and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways are kept clear.

10. Every proposal, approval, restock booking, rework order, scrap transfer and write-off is recorded with both identities and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms units awaiting approval, approved restock still to be put away, rework in progress, scrap awaiting disposal, and cage weight against the limit, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Damaged goods and quarantine
text:
1. All damaged, suspect, expired and non-conforming goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. This applies whether damage is found in Zone A, B, C, D, E or F, during receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch, cycle counts or returns inspection. No damaged pallet waits until the next shift.

2. Quarantine is located only in the marked quarantine area in Zone F. No quarantine stock is held in Zone A, Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone D staging, Zone E cold zone, the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, transit lanes or the yard. Any damaged pallet found outside quarantine is secured, marked and moved the same day.

3. Quarantined pallets are physically separated, clearly marked with cause, date, source zone and finder identity, and system-blocked as not available in the warehouse management system on the handheld WMS scanners. Blocked stock is never picked, replenished, packed, staged in Zone D, loaded or restocked until a disposition decision is recorded.

4. The finder secures the area and reports immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. The shift supervisor checks the segregation, confirms system blocking, initiates incident review, and directs spill response under PR-13 for hazmat or cleaning and cold-chain hold under PR-12 for chilled goods. The area stays secured until cleared.

5. Returns staff, inbound operators, pickers and stock controllers place goods into quarantine but do not decide their fate. The four returns and packing staff record quantity, product, batch or expiry, value and cause on the scanner. Inspection of quarantined goods takes place only in Zone F and every unit is inspected individually, without sampling.

6. Final disposition is restock, rework or scrap. Only units in original, intact, clean, correctly labelled and in-date condition are released back via booking to Zone B, Zone E or the hazmat cage. Rework takes place only in value-added packing in Zone F with re-inspection. All other units remain blocked for scrap and disposal.

7. Write-off authority follows the fixed 500 EUR threshold per case. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold.

8. Every write-off is documented with cause, quantity, value, delivery or location reference, both count identities and approval identity. Damaged goods found during daily cycle counts or the annual wall-to-wall stocktake are quarantined the same day and no adjustment is posted without a second count. No stocktake is closed without sign-off by the warehouse manager.

9. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg in quarantine movements. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, leaking or unreadable pallets are not stacked, not block-stacked above 3 high and 4.0 m, and not placed in racking. Hazmat quarantine respects the 4,000 kg cage limit, at most 5 full-weight pallets, and incompatible goods are never placed together.

10. Every quarantine placement, inspection result, disposition, write-off and disposal is recorded with time and operator identity and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms quarantine quantities and causes, stock held as unavailable, write-offs awaiting approval above 500 EUR, and any spill or incident, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Aisles, walkways and speed limits
text:
1. Speed limits at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. are fixed and enforced on every movement. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the fenced yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet. The 5 km/h areas include all marked pedestrian zones, marked crossings, pedestrian walkway interfaces and the dock ramps at doors 1-8.

2. The limits apply to all powered trucks: the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, the 8 electric pallet jacks, and any other powered equipment. Hand pallet jacks on foot are operated at walking pace and stop at crossings. No instruction, time pressure or shift target overrides a speed limit.

3. Main transport aisles through the hall are 4.0 m wide. They connect Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services, and continue to the dock doors. They are kept fully clear of pallets, staged goods, film, cardboard and waste at all times, and are never used for staging, counting or packing.

4. Rack storage aisles between the high bays in Zone B and at flow racks in Zone C are 3.0 m wide. They are kept clear of reserve pallets, replenishment units, picking carts and waste during put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, picking under PR-04 and counting under PR-08. Blocked aisles stop work until cleared.

5. Pedestrian walkways inside the hall are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from truck routes by yellow barriers. All movement on foot uses only these walkways and the marked crossings. Shortcuts through transport aisles, rack storage aisles, dock aprons, staging lanes in Zone A and Zone D, and the rear supply aisles of Zone C are prohibited.

6. Barriers, markings and crossings are safety equipment and must not be removed, moved or obscured. The maintenance technician maintains barriers, floor markings, signs and mirrors, and logs every repair. Any damaged barrier, faded marking, blocked sightline or missing sign is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, who blocks the affected route until repaired.

7. Pedestrians have priority in all marked pedestrian zones, at crossings and on dock ramps. Powered trucks reduce to 5 km/h on approach, stop where required under PR-10 and PR-11, and proceed only when the route is clear. Pedestrians make eye contact with the driver and wait until the truck has stopped before stepping onto the crossing.

8. Speed and separation are monitored on every shift. The shift supervisor on duty stops speeding, barrier breaches, aisle blocking and walking outside walkways immediately. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor, and truck horns, lights and mirrors are used at every junction and crossing.

9. Ramps, dock interfaces and mixed zones are driven at 5 km/h with particular caution. Levellers at the 1.2 m dock doors are operated only by trained warehouse staff, doors are kept closed until the truck is docked, and no pallet, cage or jack is left on ramps, crossings or walkway exits. Condensation, spillage and debris are cleaned and reported immediately.

10. Every breach of limits, aisle discipline or walkway discipline is recorded as an incident, reviewed by the shift supervisor and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms open aisle blocks, barrier damage, near misses and enforcement action, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Yard, docks and ramps
text:
1. The fenced yard of approximately 3,500 m2 is a controlled traffic area. It contains the dock apron at the 8 dock doors, the marked manoeuvring area for trailers and vans, marked pedestrian routes, and the marked driver waiting area. No other storage, staging or parking takes place in the yard outside marked areas.

2. Yard movements run only on dispatcher assignment. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific door and time slot, sequences arrivals for doors 1-4Inbound and departures for doors 5-8, and calls trucks from the waiting area only when the door and Zone A or Zone D are ready. No truck moves to a door without dispatcher instruction.

3. Door directions are fixed and enforced. Doors 1-4 are inbound only for receiving, unloading and returns receipt. Doors 5-8 are outbound only for staging release, loading and sealing. No inbound truck is directed to doors 5-8, no outbound truck to doors 1-4, and no loading or unloading takes place at any other point of the building.

4. The general speed limit in the yard is 15 km/h. It is reduced to 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including marked pedestrian zones, marked crossings, walkway interfaces and all dock ramps and aprons at doors 1-8. The 5 km/h limit is enforced and no time pressure overrides it.

5. Trailers and vans manoeuvre only on the marked manoeuvring area and dock apron under dispatcher and shift supervisor direction. Reversing to the door is performed only after the call to the door, at walking pace with mirrors, lights and horn. The dock apron, transport aisles and pedestrian routes are kept fully clear and are never used for waiting or staging.

6. Each of the 8 dock doors is at 1.2 m dock height and has its own leveller. Levellers are operated only by trained warehouse staff, never by drivers. The door is kept closed until the assigned truck is correctly docked and secured, the leveller is then placed, and after loading or unloading the leveller is removed, the door closed and the departure recorded.

7. Drivers report to the yard entrance on arrival, announce booking reference and assigned door, then move only to the marked waiting area and wait there until called. Drivers remain in the waiting area, use only marked pedestrian routes on foot, and never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or Zone F. Drivers take no part in unloading, loading, counting, wrapping or sealing.

8. On docking the driver secures the vehicle, switches off the engine where required, hands over documents at the cab or door interface, and returns to the waiting area. Engine restart and pull-off take place only on dispatcher instruction after leveller removal, door closure, seal check and document handover. Unbooked, early or late trucks wait in the waiting area until re-sequenced.

9. Pedestrians in the yard have priority and use only the marked pedestrian routes, walkways and crossings. Powered trucks reduce to 5 km/h on approach to crossings and ramps and stop where required under PR-10 and PR-11. No pallet, cage, jack, film or waste is left on ramps, aprons, crossings or walkway exits, and spillage, ice and debris are cleaned and reported immediately.

10. Every arrival, door change, time-slot deviation, leveller fault, waiting time and open load is recorded by the dispatcher and reviewed by the shift supervisor. Yard blocks, door faults, near misses and breaches of door discipline are treated as incidents. Open trucks, rebooked slots and door readiness are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15 with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Pedestrian protection and PPE
text:
1. Every person on the warehouse floor wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times, with no exceptions. This applies to the warehouse manager, shift supervisors, forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, maintenance technician, dispatchers and floaters, and to any authorised visitor or contractor while on the floor.

2. High-visibility vests are worn closed and fully visible over other clothing, not carried, tied around the waist or covered by jackets. Class S3 safety footwear is worn correctly laced, in serviceable condition with intact toe caps and soles. Any person without correct vest and footwear leaves the floor immediately and reports to the shift supervisor, and work does not start or continue without full PPE.

3. All movement on foot inside the hall uses only the physically separated pedestrian walkways and marked crossings under PR-11 Pedestrian safety. The walkways are 1.2 m wide and are protected from truck routes by yellow barriers. Shortcuts through main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m, dock aprons, staging lanes in Zone A and Zone D, and rear supply aisles in Zone C are prohibited.

4. Barriers, floor markings, signs and mirrors are safety equipment. They must not be removed, moved, obscured or climbed over. The maintenance technician maintains barriers and markings and logs every repair. Any damaged barrier, faded marking, blocked sightline or missing sign is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, who blocks the affected route until repaired.

5. Pedestrians have absolute priority in all marked pedestrian zones, at marked crossings, on walkway interfaces and on dock ramps. Powered trucks reduce to 5 km/h on approach and stop where required under PR-10 and PR-11. Pedestrians make eye contact with the driver and wait until the truck has fully stopped before stepping onto the crossing.

6. Forklift operators and drivers of any other powered truck wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. The belt is fastened before moving off and remains fastened until the truck is fully stopped and secured. Trucks use horn, lights and mirrors at every junction, crossing and Zone C interface. Non-compliance is stopped immediately by the shift supervisor.

7. Separation between people and trucks is enforced by speed and distance. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and 8 electric pallet jacks never overtake pedestrians in walkway zones and never park on crossings, ramps or walkway exits.

8. Drivers and external carriers are never pedestrians in the hall. Drivers wait only in the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard until called to their assigned door, use only marked pedestrian routes on foot in the yard, and never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or Zone F. Inbound work uses doors 1-4 and outbound work uses doors 5-8 only.

9. Pedestrian areas are kept fully clear at all times. No pallet, cage, jack, film, cardboard or waste is left on the 1.2 m walkways, crossings, ramps or walkway exits, and main transport aisles of 4.0 m are never used for staging. Condensation, spillage, ice and debris are cleaned immediately and reported to the shift supervisor, with chilled and hazmat spills secured under PR-12 and PR-13.

10. Every breach of barrier, walkway, priority or PPE discipline is recorded as an incident, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor on duty, and enforced before work resumes. Open blocks, barrier damage, near misses and enforcement action are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Electric fleet overview
text:
1. The handling fleet at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. is all electric. No diesel, gas or petrol trucks are used inside the hall or in the yard. The fleet consists of powered trucks for lifting and transport, manual jacks for small moves, and shared fixed equipment for wrapping, baling, docking and scanning.

2. Six counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t provide general work across the site. They serve unloading and loading at the 1.2 m dock doors, collection from Zone A, transfer by the 4.0 m main transport aisles, staging to Zone D, and feeding of the Zone B transfer lanes. They do not work inside the high-bay racking aisles.

3. Four reach trucks rated at 1.6 t serve the high bays in Zone B bulk storage. They perform put-away to the 2,400 pallet positions, replenishment release to Zone C, and work in the 3.0 m rack storage aisles. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and the reach rating is built on the site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg.

4. Eight electric pallet jacks cover horizontal moves, dock work and replenishment support. They are used in Zone A receiving lanes, Zone C rear supply aisles, Zone D staging lanes for doors 5-8, and transfers to Zone E and Zone F. They are driven only by authorised forklift operators with seat belts where fitted and daily check completed.

5. Twelve hand pallet jacks are provided for small moves on foot. They are used by forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers and packing staff for positioning pallets, feeding packing areas and clearing lanes. They are operated at walking pace, never ridden, and are stopped at crossings and walkway interfaces.

6. Two semi-automatic stretch wrappers secure all outbound pallets. They are located at the packing and Zone D interface and are operated only by instructed packing and forklift staff. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D, and unstable wraps are re-wrapped before loading to trailers of 22,000 kg or the van of 1,200 kg.

7. One cardboard baler handles all cardboard, carton and packaging waste from picking in Zone C, packing and value-added packing in Zone F. It is operated only by instructed staff, with main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack aisles of 3.0 m and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways kept clear of waste at all times.

8. Each of the 8 dock doors has its own leveller for the 1.2 m dock height. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only. Levellers are operated only by trained warehouse staff, never by drivers, and are placed only after the assigned truck is docked and secured and removed before departure.

9. Twenty handheld WMS scanners are shared across shifts for all system tasks. They control booking in Zone A, put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, scan-verified picking under PR-04, packing confirmation under PR-05, release and loading under PR-06, returns under PR-07, and cycle counts under PR-08. No task runs without an active scanner task.

10. All trucks, wrappers, baler, levellers and scanners are maintained by the maintenance technician, with every repair logged. Trucks receive a documented check before first use each day under PR-10, racking receives a documented inspection every month, and faults affecting safety or load capacity block the equipment until cleared and handed over under PR-15.

title: Authorisation and daily checks
text:
1. No licence, no truck. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks are driven only by personally authorised operators. No employee operates any powered truck without prior personal authorisation, and no assignment, instruction or time pressure replaces it.

2. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators. The authorisation is individual, recorded by name, truck type and date, and is a precondition for any truck assignment. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and other staff cannot authorise operators, and unauthorised driving is stopped immediately by the shift supervisor on duty.

3. Authorisation is type-specific and task-bound. Counterbalance work across Zone A, Zone D and the 4.0 m main transport aisles, high-bay work with reach trucks in the 3.0 m rack aisles of Zone B, and dock and transfer work with electric pallet jacks each require the corresponding authorisation. An operator authorised only for one type does not drive another type.

4. The 8 forklift operators hold powered-truck authorisations and perform all put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, staging to Zone D and loading and unloading at the 1.2 m dock doors. No other role operates forklifts or reach trucks. The 12 hand pallet jacks are used on foot for small moves by instructed inbound operators, pickers, packing staff and floaters at walking pace.

5. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. The check is performed by the authorised operator assigned to the truck for that shift, using the 20 handheld WMS scanners or the check form where directed, with truck identity, date, time and operator identity recorded.

6. The daily check covers brakes, steering, horn, lights, mirrors, seat belt, forks and carriage, wheels and tyres, battery charge and charger cable condition, hydraulic leaks, emergency stop and warning decals. For reach trucks it includes reach, tilt and height functions in the high bays. For electric pallet jacks it includes tiller, drive, lift and lowering controls. Levellers, wrappers and scanners used that day are checked for evident faults.

7. A truck with any safety fault, brake, steering, belt, horn, light, fork, chain, hydraulic or battery defect, or with unreadable rating plate, is blocked immediately. The operator tags the truck as not for use, parks it clear of the 4.0 m aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, crossings and the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways, and reports to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician before any further use.

8. The maintenance technician owns the condition of trucks, racking and dock equipment and logs every repair. Faults affecting safety or load capacity block the truck until inspected, repaired and cleared in the log. The 2,700 kg bay limit, the 800 kg pallet limit and the 2.5 t and 1.6 t truck ratings are never exceeded to compensate for a faulty truck.

9. The shift supervisor on duty verifies authorisations and daily checks before allocating work. No scanner task under PR-02, PR-03, PR-04, PR-05 or PR-06 is assigned to an unauthorised operator or to an unchecked or blocked truck. Seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving, and limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are enforced.

10. Authorisations, checks, blocks and repairs are recorded for follow-up and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms which trucks are in service, which are blocked for repair, which checks are outstanding for the next shift, and any incident or near miss, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Safe operation rules
text:
1. Powered trucks are driven only by personally authorised operators on active WMS scanner tasks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. No licence, no truck: the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks are never driven without warehouse manager authorisation and a documented check before first use each day.

2. Seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving. The belt is fastened before moving off, remains fastened during all travel, lifting, reversing and ramp work, and is released only after the truck is fully stopped, lowered and secured. Trucks with a defective belt are blocked, tagged as not for use and reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician.

3. Speed limits are fixed and enforced on all routes. The limit is 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the fenced yard of 3,500 m2, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, including marked pedestrian zones, marked crossings, walkway interfaces and dock ramps at doors 1-8. No shift plan, delay or instruction overrides a limit.

4. Trucks run only on defined routes and keep separation from people at all times. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m are used for travel between Zone A, B, C, D, E and F, and 3.0 m rack storage aisles only for assigned high-bay work. The 1.2 m walkways physically separated by yellow barriers are never driven on, blocked or used for staging.

5. Pedestrians have priority under PR-11. Trucks reduce to 5 km/h on approach to crossings and ramps, stop where required, and proceed only when the route is clear. Horn, lights and mirrors are used at every junction, crossing and Zone C interface. The driver makes eye contact with pedestrians and never overtakes pedestrians in walkway zones.

6. Loads are handled only within fixed limits. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. Only stable, fully supported, wrapped pallets with readable labels are lifted. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, damaged or unreadable pallets are refused and reported.

7. High-bay and dock work follows type discipline. The 4 reach trucks work in the 3.0 m high-bay aisles of Zone B, the 6 counterbalance trucks feed transfer lanes and doors, and electric pallet jacks cover horizontal and dock moves. Forks are kept low during travel, high only for placement, and no person is ever lifted, carried or allowed under raised forks.

8. Levellers at the 1.2 m dock doors, the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and the 1 cardboard baler are operated only by trained and instructed staff. Levellers are placed only after the assigned truck is docked and secured and removed before departure. Trucks are parked only in marked areas, lowered, switched off and secured, never on aisles, crossings, ramps or walkway exits.

9. The 12 hand pallet jacks are operated on foot at walking pace by instructed staff for small moves. They are never ridden, never pulled across crossings without stopping, and never left in aisles or on ramps. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for every operator and pedestrian on the floor, and drivers never enter the hall.

10. Every speeding, belt, overload, impact, near miss or equipment fault is stopped immediately, secured and reported to the shift supervisor on duty, who reviews the incident report and blocks truck or bay until cleared. Truck status, blocks, repairs logged by the maintenance technician and enforcement action are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15 with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Evacuation and drills
text:
1. Emergency evacuation is performed under PR-14 Emergency evacuation and applies to everyone on site. This includes all floor staff, the warehouse manager, the shift supervisor on duty, dispatchers, the maintenance technician, and any authorised visitor, contractor or driver present in the yard. Safety, PPE and evacuation instructions from the shift supervisor are binding.

2. Any alarm, fire, smoke, gas suspicion, spill with vapour risk, structural damage, rack collapse or other immediate danger triggers evacuation. The person discovering the danger stops work, secures equipment where safe to do so, alerts nearby staff, activates the nearest alarm call point, and reports immediately to the shift supervisor on duty.

3. On alarm all handling, picking, packing, loading and counting stop at once. Powered trucks are stopped, lowered and secured clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and crossings where possible. Dock levellers at the 1.2 m doors are left in place, doors are not blocked, and no pallet, jack or wrapper is moved to the exits.

4. Everyone leaves the hall immediately by the marked escape routes on foot. Only the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways and marked crossings and exits are used for escape, moving away from the danger to the outside. Lifts, trucks, hand pallet jacks and personal belongings are not used or collected. Pedestrians keep priority discipline and move at a brisk walk without running.

5. Drivers in the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard do not enter the hall and do not move trucks. On alarm they leave vehicles where safely parked, move on foot by the marked pedestrian routes to the assembly point, and follow dispatcher and shift supervisor instructions. No vehicle enters or leaves the yard during evacuation.

6. The assembly point is at the marked area by the north fence outside the hall. All evacuated persons assemble there by shift, zone and role, clear of dock aprons, manoeuvring areas and access routes for emergency services. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain worn, and the area is kept clear of pallets, equipment and waste.

7. Roll call is performed at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor on duty conducts the roll call against the shift attendance, handover record, visitor log and dispatcher driver list for the morning shift 06:00-14:00, afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, or approved Saturday morning overtime. Missing persons are reported immediately to emergency services and the warehouse manager.

8. No one re-enters the hall, yard work areas or dock ramps until the roll call is complete and re-entry is explicitly authorised. The shift supervisor confirms the count, secures the building against re-entry, and releases the building only after clearance by emergency services or, for drills and false alarms, by the shift supervisor with the warehouse manager informed. Partial re-entry is prohibited.

9. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. Each drill covers alarm activation, escape by marked routes, truck securing, yard control, assembly by the north fence, and roll call before authorised re-entry. The shift supervisors alternate drill timing across mornings, afternoons and, where applicable, Saturday overtime, so all 38 to 40 staff practise.

10. Every alarm, evacuation, drill and failed roll call is recorded with date, time, zones involved, attendance count, findings and corrective actions, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. Barrier, marking, alarm and exit faults found during drills are logged for the maintenance technician and block the route until repaired.

title: Safety inspections and incidents
text:
1. Safety on site is controlled by two fixed routines: documented monthly inspection of racking and equipment, and immediate reporting and review of every incident. Both routines apply during the Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 and during approved Saturday morning overtime, and both are enforced by the shift supervisor on duty.

2. Racking is subject to documented safety inspection every month under PR-08 and PR-10. The maintenance technician inspects all high-bay racking in Zone B with 2,400 positions, flow racks in Zone C, and positions in Zone E, including uprights, beams, beam locks, bracing, floor fixings and bay labels. The result is recorded with date, area, findings and signature.

3. Every repair to trucks, racking and dock equipment is logged by the maintenance technician. The log records truck identity or bay reference, fault description, date and time found, person reporting, repair performed and clearance for reuse. Faults affecting safety or load capacity block the truck or bay until inspected, repaired and cleared.

4. Any impact, deformation, cracked upright, loose beam, missing lock, overload evidence, falling material or damaged pallet in racking is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The affected bay is blocked, unloaded if required, and secured against put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03 and picking under PR-04 until cleared by the maintenance technician.

5. Every incident is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. This includes damage, near miss, spill, rack impact, truck fault, leveller fault, barrier damage, temperature alarm in Zone E, hazmat leak, breach of the 500 EUR write-off discipline and any personal injury. The finder stops work, secures the area and does not move goods or equipment until released.

6. The shift supervisor leads the immediate response under the relevant procedure: PR-09 for damaged goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day, PR-12 for cold-chain hold between +2 °C and +8 °C, PR-13 for hazmat spill containment in the 60 m2 cage, PR-10 and PR-11 for truck and pedestrian protection, and PR-14 for evacuation and assembly by the north fence. Instructions on safety, PPE and evacuation are binding.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Each report records date, time, zone, door from doors 1-8 where applicable, persons and trucks involved, cause, damage and quantity, with high-visibility vest, class S3 footwear and seat-belt compliance noted. The supervisor checks segregation, system blocking on the handheld WMS scanners, quarantine transfer and speed compliance at 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps.

8. Reports requiring decisions above supervisor authority are escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift. This includes write-offs above 500 EUR, stocktake discrepancies, cage loads against the 4,000 kg limit, bay overloads against the 2,700 kg limit, pallets above 800 kg, and any injury or structural damage. No escalated incident is closed without warehouse manager decision.

9. Barriers, markings, alarms and exits are checked as part of every inspection and after every incident. The 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, mirrors, signs, dock levellers at 1.2 m height, spill and fire equipment are kept clear and serviceable. Any defect blocks the route or equipment until repaired and logged.

10. Every inspection, repair, blocked bay, blocked truck, incident report, review and escalation is recorded and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms bays and trucks blocked, quarantine quantities, open investigations and corrective actions, with clear ownership for the incoming shift until every point is cleared.

title: Cold-chain and hazmat controls
text:
1. Zone E — cold zone of 300 m2 is held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. The range applies during the morning shift 06:00-14:00, the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, approved Saturday morning overtime and outside operating hours. Doors, curtains, seals and cooling equipment are kept closed and serviceable, and doors are opened only for put-away, replenishment and counting tasks.

2. Zone E is equipped with continuous temperature monitoring and alarms. Any alarm, deviation outside +2 °C to +8 °C, cooling fault, door fault, sensor fault or power interruption is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. The affected area is secured, affected stock is system-blocked as not available on the handheld WMS scanners, and no chilled pallet is picked, replenished, packed or dispatched until cleared.

3. A manual temperature verification is performed in Zone E on each shift. The morning shift and the afternoon shift each record the reading, time, device identity and operator identity, and the shift supervisor reviews and countersigns the record. A missing or failed verification stops all chilled movements until a verified reading back in range is recorded.

4. Chilled put-away and replenishment follow PR-02, PR-03 and PR-12 without delay or intermediate staging. Chilled pallets are booked in Zone A only after document check, count and inspection, moved directly to Zone E, and returned to Zone E immediately after counting. Exposure time outside the cold zone is kept to the minimum, and condensation, spillage and damaged insulation are cleaned and reported immediately.

5. Chilled pallets with broken cold-chain evidence, damaged insulation, missing batch or expiry data, or any pallet, load included, above 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged or unreadable are not stored as available stock. They are segregated, reported to the shift supervisor, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Chilled returns are handled only in Zone F with minimum exposure time.

6. Hazmat is stored only in the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Total storage never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time, which is at most 5 full-weight pallets of 800 kg. No hazmat sits in Zone A, B, C, D or E, in transit lanes, on dock aprons or in the yard, and no task is released from Zone A that would exceed the limit.

7. Every hazmat placement and removal is scan-verified by source and target, with labelling, closure, seals, leakage checks and compatibility confirmed. Incompatible goods are never placed together. Ventilation, segregation, spill containment, fire and emergency equipment at the cage are kept clear and serviceable, and access is limited to instructed staff under the shift supervisor.

8. Any leak, damaged seal, missing hazard label, spill, vapour suspicion or cage alarm stops work immediately. The finder stops handling, secures the area, alerts nearby staff and reports to the shift supervisor. The supervisor initiates spill containment under PR-13, directs PPE, ventilation and evacuation under PR-14 where required, and blocks the cage, truck or bay until cleared by the maintenance technician.

9. Contaminated, leaking and suspect hazmat goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. They are physically separated, clearly marked, system-blocked as not available, and never picked, replenished, packed or staged in Zone D. Write-offs follow the 500 EUR authority rule, with the shift supervisor approving up to 500 EUR and the warehouse manager approving above 500 EUR.

10. Every temperature reading, alarm, deviation, cage movement against the 4,000 kg limit, spill, quarantine transfer and open investigation is recorded with time and operator identity and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms last verified temperature, alarm status, cage weight and pallets on hand, and stock held as unavailable, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: End-of-shift handover
text:
1. End-of-shift handover is performed under PR-15 at every shift change. The outgoing shift supervisor hands over to the incoming shift supervisor at 14:00 between the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, and at 22:00 from the afternoon shift to the next morning shift. Handover during approved Saturday morning overtime follows the same discipline.

2. The handover is documented and signed by both supervisors with date, time and identities. Verbal exchange alone is not sufficient. The record is kept with the shift papers, uses the handheld WMS scanner data where directed, and is the binding proof of which loads, zones and issues have been transferred with clear ownership. No open point is carried silently.

3. Dock and yard status is handed over by door and booking. The record confirms carriers at inbound doors 1-4 and outbound doors 5-8, trucks still in the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard, time-slot deviations, door changes, rebooked slots and leveller faults at the 1.2 m doors. The dispatcher booking list and waiting times are attached.

4. Inbound and outbound loads are handed over by delivery and pallet. The record confirms which inbound loads in Zone A are booked, released and awaiting put-away to Zone B, E or F, which deliveries are still held for documents, count or inspection, which pallets are staged in the 900 m2 Zone D by door and load, and which loads are released, loaded, sealed or still pending correction.

5. Storage, replenishment and picking status is handed over by zone and task. The record confirms put-away tasks completed and uncompleted under PR-02, pick faces in Zone C replenished and released under PR-03 before the next picking shift, open orders and short picks under PR-04, packed and wrapped pallets under PR-05, and blocked bays, missing labels and rack damage for the maintenance technician.

6. Inventory control status is handed over for stock controller follow-up. The record confirms daily cycle counts completed by rotating zone, locations blocked for second count or recount, prepared adjustments awaiting approval, and the freeze and release state during the annual wall-to-wall stocktake. No adjustment is posted without a second count, and the warehouse manager signs off the stocktake.

7. Cold-chain status in the 300 m2 Zone E is handed over with the last manual temperature verification of the shift. The record confirms the reading, time, device and operator identity, alarm status, deviations outside +2 °C to +8 °C, stock held as not available, and pallets still awaiting put-away or replenishment with minimum exposure time under PR-12.

8. Hazmat, quarantine and returns status in Zone F is handed over with weights and causes. The record confirms current cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit and pallets on hand against the 5 full-weight equivalent, quarantine quantities, causes and system blocking, returns received, inspected and awaiting disposition approval, rework in progress, scrap awaiting disposal, and write-offs within the 500 EUR authority rule.

9. Equipment, safety and incidents are handed over with blocks and actions. The record confirms which of the 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks and 8 electric pallet jacks are in service, blocked or awaiting daily check, barrier and marking damage, breaches of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps, and every incident report reviewed by the outgoing supervisor with response and escalation.

10. The incoming shift supervisor accepts the floor only after the record is complete and all open points have an owner. Unresolved discrepancies, unreleased pallets, blocked trucks or bays, and escalations above 500 EUR, above 800 kg per pallet or above bay and cage limits are taken over explicitly and reported to the warehouse manager the same shift. Work restarts only on this accepted handover.

title: Speed limits and shared areas
text:
1. Speed limits at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. are fixed, enforced and apply to every powered truck on every shift. No instruction, delay, shift target or time pressure overrides a limit. The limits apply to the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks under PR-10 and PR-11.

2. Inside the building the limit is 8 km/h. This covers all travel in the 6,000 m2 hall, including the 4.0 m main transport aisles between Zones A to F, the transfer lanes, the Zone D staging lanes and the interfaces to the dock doors. Trucks exceeding 8 km/h inside are stopped immediately by the shift supervisor.

3. In the fenced yard of 3,500 m2 the limit is 15 km/h. This covers the dock apron at the 8 dock doors, the marked manoeuvring area for trailers and vans, and travel between the yard entrance, the marked driver waiting area and the doors. Reversing to a door is performed at walking pace with lights, mirrors and horn.

4. Wherever people and trucks meet the limit is 5 km/h. This covers all marked pedestrian zones, all marked crossings and walkway interfaces inside the hall and in the yard, and all dock ramps and aprons at doors 1-8. The 5 km/h limit applies in addition to the 8 km/h and 15 km/h limits and governs on approach, on crossings and on ramps.

5. Hand pallet jacks are operated on foot at walking pace only. The 12 hand pallet jacks stop at every crossing and walkway interface, are never ridden and never pulled across a crossing without stopping. Walking pace does not replace the 5 km/h rule for powered trucks operating in the same area.

6. Pedestrians have priority in all shared areas. In every marked pedestrian zone, at every marked crossing and on every dock ramp, the powered truck gives way to the person on foot. The driver reduces to 5 km/h on approach, stops where required, and proceeds only when the route is fully clear.

7. Priority is exercised jointly. The pedestrian uses only the 1.2 m walkways physically separated by yellow barriers and the marked crossings, makes eye contact with the driver, and waits until the truck has fully stopped before stepping onto the crossing. The driver confirms eye contact and keeps the truck stopped until the pedestrian has cleared the area.

8. Shared areas are kept clear and visible at all times. No pallet, cage, jack, film, cardboard or waste is left on walkways, crossings, ramps, apron exits or sightlines. Barriers, floor markings, signs and mirrors must not be removed, moved or obscured. Any damage, blocked sightline or spillage is reported immediately to the shift supervisor.

9. Forklift operators wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving and use horn, lights and mirrors at every junction, crossing and Zone C interface. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the floor. Trucks never overtake pedestrians in walkway zones and never park on crossings, ramps or walkway exits.

10. Every speeding event, priority breach, barrier breach or near miss in a shared area is recorded as an incident and reviewed by the shift supervisor on duty. Findings, blocks and enforcement action are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for the incoming shift until cleared.

title: Walkways, aisles and dock areas
text:
1. Pedestrian walkways inside the 6,000 m2 hall are physically separated from all truck routes by yellow barriers. The walkways are 1.2 m wide and are the only permitted routes for movement on foot. No person walks on transport aisles, rack aisles, dock aprons or staging lanes.

2. Walkways connect all working areas between Zones A to F, the office annex, the exits and the yard interfaces via marked crossings. All crossings are marked, signed and kept visible with mirrors where directed. Pedestrians cross truck routes only at these crossings and only after eye contact and a full stop of the truck.

3. Main transport aisles through the hall are 4.0 m wide. They link Zone A receiving, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C picking, Zone D dispatch, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services to the dock doors. They are kept fully clear of pallets, staged goods, film, cardboard and waste and are never used for staging, packing or counting.

4. Rack storage aisles in Zone B and at the flow racks in Zone C are 3.0 m wide. They are used only for assigned put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, picking under PR-04 and counting under PR-08. Reserve pallets, picking carts and waste are never left in these aisles, and a blocked aisle stops work until cleared.

5. Barriers, floor markings, signs and mirrors are safety equipment under PR-11. They must not be removed, moved, obscured, climbed over or driven through. The maintenance technician maintains them and logs every repair. Any damaged barrier, faded marking or blocked sightline is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, who blocks the route until repaired.

6. The building is served by 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own leveller. Doors 1-4 are inbound only for Zone A and returns receipt, doors 5-8 are outbound only for Zone D. No inbound work takes place at doors 5-8, no outbound work at doors 1-4, and no loading or unloading takes place elsewhere.

7. Levellers are operated only by trained warehouse staff, never by drivers. The door stays closed until the assigned truck is correctly docked and secured, the leveller is then placed, and after handling it is removed and the door closed. No pallet, jack, cage or wrapper is left on ramps, aprons or walkway exits.

8. The fenced yard of 3,500 m2 is a controlled traffic area with dock apron, marked manoeuvring area, marked pedestrian routes and the marked driver waiting area. Yard travel is 15 km/h, reduced to 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and all dock ramps and aprons. Reversing to a door is at walking pace on dispatcher call only.

9. Drivers never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or Zone F and take no part in unloading, loading, counting, wrapping or sealing. After reporting at the yard entrance with booking reference and assigned door and time slot, the driver waits only in the marked waiting area, uses only marked pedestrian routes on foot, and moves to the door only when called by the dispatcher.

10. Every breach of walkway, aisle, door or waiting-area discipline is recorded as an incident and reviewed by the shift supervisor on duty. Open aisle blocks, barrier damage, door and leveller faults, waiting times and enforcement action are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Driver authorisation and truck checks
text:
1. No licence, no truck. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks are driven only by personally authorised operators on active scanner tasks under PR-10. No assignment, instruction, delay or time pressure replaces authorisation.

2. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators. The authorisation is individual and recorded by name, truck type and date, and is a precondition for any truck assignment by the shift supervisor. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and other staff cannot authorise operators.

3. Authorisation is type-specific and task-bound. General work with counterbalance trucks across Zone A, the 4.0 m main aisles and Zone D, high-bay work with reach trucks in the 3.0 m rack aisles of Zone B, and horizontal and dock work with electric pallet jacks each require the corresponding authorisation. An operator authorised for one type does not drive another type.

4. The 8 forklift operators hold powered-truck authorisations and perform all powered handling. This covers put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03, staging to Zone D, and loading and unloading at the 1.2 m dock doors. No other role operates forklifts, reach trucks or electric pallet jacks.

5. The 12 hand pallet jacks are not powered trucks. They are used on foot at walking pace for small moves by instructed inbound operators, pickers, packing staff, returns staff and floaters. They are never ridden, never pulled across a marked crossing without stopping, and never left in aisles, on ramps or at walkway exits.

6. Capacities are fixed and never exceeded to compensate for planning or faulty equipment. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, counterbalance trucks are rated at 2.5 t and reach trucks at 1.6 t. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, damaged or unreadable pallets are refused and reported.

7. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10. The check is performed by the authorised operator assigned to the truck for that shift, with truck identity, date, time and operator identity recorded on the check form or WMS scanner where directed.

8. The daily check covers brakes, steering, horn, lights, mirrors, seat belt, forks and carriage, chains, wheels and tyres, battery charge and charger cable condition, hydraulic leaks, emergency stop and rating plate legibility. For reach trucks it includes reach, tilt and height functions. For electric pallet jacks it includes tiller, drive, lift and lowering controls.

9. A truck with any safety fault is blocked immediately. Brake, steering, belt, horn, light, fork, chain, hydraulic or battery defects, unreadable rating plates and evident faults on levellers, wrappers or scanners stop use. The operator tags the truck as not for use, parks it clear of the 4.0 m aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, crossings and 1.2 m walkways, and reports to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician.

10. The shift supervisor verifies authorisations and daily checks before allocating work and enforces seat belts, with the belt fastened whenever the truck is moving. The maintenance technician logs every repair and clears blocked trucks and bays for reuse. Authorisations, checks, blocks and repairs are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

title: Required PPE and seat belts
text:
1. Every person on the warehouse floor wears a high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times, with no exceptions. This applies on the morning shift 06:00-14:00, the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 and approved Saturday morning overtime, in all Zones A to F, on all aisles, walkways, dock ramps and staging areas inside the 6,000 m2 hall.

2. The rule covers all roles on site: the warehouse manager, the shift supervisor on duty, the 8 forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, the maintenance technician, dispatchers and floaters. It also covers any authorised visitor, contractor or other person while on the floor. No work starts or continues without full PPE.

3. High-visibility vests are worn closed and fully visible over other clothing. They are not carried in the hand, tied around the waist, worn open or covered by jackets or other garments. A vest that is dirty, damaged or no longer reflective is replaced immediately and reported to the shift supervisor.

4. Class S3 safety footwear is worn correctly laced, fully closed and in serviceable condition, with intact toe caps, soles and fastenings. Damaged, open, unlaced or makeshift footwear is not permitted on the floor. Spare vests and replacement footwear discipline is enforced before entry to the floor, not after work has started.

5. Any person without correct vest and footwear leaves the floor immediately and reports to the shift supervisor on duty. The shift supervisor stops the work concerned, blocks the task on the handheld WMS scanner where applicable, and permits return only when full PPE is worn. Instructions on PPE are binding for everyone on site under PR-11.

6. Forklift operators and drivers of any other powered truck wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. This covers the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks where a belt is fitted. No assignment, delay or time pressure replaces the belt.

7. The seat belt is fastened before moving off and remains fastened during all travel, lifting, reach, tilt, reversing and ramp work at the 1.2 m dock doors. It is released only after the truck is fully stopped, forks lowered and the truck secured. Trucks run only after the documented check before first use each day under PR-10, including belt condition.

8. A truck with a defective, missing or unreadable seat belt is blocked immediately. The operator tags the truck as not for use, parks it clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack aisles, crossings and the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways, and reports to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. A blocked truck is not returned to service until repaired and logged as cleared.

9. PPE and seat-belt discipline applies together with speed and separation rules. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet, use horn, lights and mirrors at every junction and crossing, and give way to pedestrians. High-visibility vests do not replace eye contact, full stop and priority discipline in shared areas.

10. Every breach of vest, footwear or seat-belt discipline is recorded as an incident and reviewed by the shift supervisor on duty. The report notes date, time, zone, persons and trucks involved and corrective action, with enforcement before work resumes. Open breaches and enforcement action are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Racking and stacking limits
text:
1. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. This is the fixed site standard for every rack, truck and stack. It covers pallet, goods, packaging, film and label combined. No pallet exceeding 800 kg is placed in racking, block-stacked, replenished or stored, and no bay limit or task plan assumes a higher weight.

2. Each rack bay in the high-bay storage carries at most 2,700 kg, including pallets and loads. The limit applies to every bay in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, at every height level and for every product type. Overloading a bay is prohibited and is stopped immediately by the shift supervisor on duty.

3. Only conforming pallets are placed in racking. Pallets must be stable, undamaged, fully supported on both beams without overhang or collapse, and carry a readable location and pallet label. Unstable, overhanging, damaged, wet or unreadable pallets are refused for racking, segregated and reported to the shift supervisor.

4. Free block-stacking outside the racking is permitted only in marked block areas in Zone B and is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m stacking height. Both limits apply together: a stack ends at 3 pallets even if below 4.0 m, and ends below 3 pallets if 4.0 m would be exceeded. Higher or taller stacks are prohibited.

5. Block stacks must be vertical, aligned and stable on sound pallets of the same footprint. Mixed footprints, leaning stacks, damaged bottom pallets, overhanging cartons and use of aisles, crossings or walkway exits for stacking are prohibited. Non-conforming stacks are broken down immediately and reported.

6. High-bay placement is performed only by authorised operators with the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, fed by the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t on the transfer lanes. Operators scan-verify bay and beam labels, check full beam support before setting down, and confirm placement on the handheld WMS scanner under PR-02 and PR-10.

7. Bay and stack limits are never overridden to fit a non-conforming pallet, to clear Zone A or to meet a shift target. Overweight, unstable or damaged pallets are held in the marked Zone A lanes and, if damaged, moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. No instruction or time pressure replaces the 800 kg, 2,700 kg and 3-high and 4.0 m limits.

8. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m, rack storage aisles of 3.0 m and pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m with yellow barriers are kept fully clear of pallets, reserve stock and waste during all racking and stacking work. Powered trucks observe 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet. No stack or pallet blocks beams, sprinklers, sensors or emergency equipment.

9. Racking is subject to documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects uprights, beams, beam locks, bracing, floor fixings and labels across Zone B, Zone C flow racks and Zone E, and records date, area, findings and signature. Every repair is logged, and faults affecting load capacity block the bay until cleared.

10. Any impact, deformation, cracked upright, loose beam, missing lock, overload evidence or falling material is reported immediately to the shift supervisor. The bay or stack is blocked, unloaded if required and secured against put-away, replenishment and picking until cleared by the maintenance technician. Findings are recorded as an incident, reviewed by the shift supervisor and transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

title: Supervision and shift handover
text:
1. The site is continuously supervised during all operating hours. On Monday to Friday the morning shift runs from 06:00 to 14:00 and the afternoon shift from 14:00 to 22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only. At any time during operations there is always exactly one shift supervisor in charge of the floor.

2. The shift supervisor on duty directs all floor staff, enforces Zones A to F discipline and procedures PR-01 to PR-15, and leads immediate response to any incident, damage, spill or evacuation. Instructions from the shift supervisor on safety, PPE, zone stops, speed limits and evacuation are binding for everyone in the 6,000 m2 hall and the 3,500 m2 yard.

3. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site across both shifts for operations, safety and final sign-offs. Matters exceeding supervisor authority, including overtime, write-offs above 500 EUR, stocktake sign-off and temporary departures from procedure, are escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift.

4. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime. No extension of the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and no Saturday morning working takes place without prior written approval. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and other staff cannot authorise overtime, and the hall stays closed and secured outside approved hours.

5. Cover is maintained so supervision and key safety functions are never left uncovered. Around 38 to 40 staff are distributed across the two shifts, with 2 floaters covering absence in inbound, picking, packing and pallet-jack moves. Counters, replenishment, dock work and truck checks are not started without supervisor cover and available labour.

6. The shift supervisor verifies safety readiness before allocating work. No scanner task is assigned to an unauthorised operator or to an unchecked or blocked truck, no work starts without high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear, and speeding, barrier breaches, aisle blocking and walking outside the 1.2 m walkways are stopped immediately.

7. Every incident is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. This includes PPE and seat-belt breaches, speeding at 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps, rack impacts, barrier damage, truck and leveller faults, temperature alarms and hazmat leaks.
