The area is secured and the report is reviewed and countersigned.

8. End-of-shift handover is performed under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00, and for approved Saturday overtime on the same discipline. The outgoing shift supervisor hands over to the incoming shift supervisor in a documented record signed by both, with date, time and identities. Verbal exchange alone is not sufficient.

9. The safety handover confirms open aisle blocks on the 4.0 m and 3.0 m aisles, barrier and marking damage, trucks in service or blocked for repair, outstanding daily checks, quarantine and hazmat cage status against the 4,000 kg limit, Zone E temperature status, and every incident report with response and escalation. Dock bookings, open loads and pending replenishment are handed over with clear ownership.

10. The incoming shift supervisor accepts the floor only after the record is complete and every open point has an owner. Unresolved blocks, unreleased pallets, blocked trucks or bays, and escalations to the warehouse manager are taken over explicitly. Work restarts only on this accepted handover, with no silent carry-over to the next shift.

title: Cold zone rules
text:
1. Zone E — cold zone occupies 300 m2 and is the only chilled store on site. It holds only inspected and booked chilled packed goods requiring storage between +2 °C and +8 °C. No ambient goods, hazmat, quarantine, returns or value-added work is placed in Zone E, and no chilled goods are stored in Zones A, B, C, D or F.

2. The temperature in Zone E is held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times. This applies on the morning shift 06:00-14:00, the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, approved Saturday morning overtime and outside operating hours. Cooling units, doors, curtains, seals and sensors are kept closed and serviceable, and doors are opened only for assigned tasks.

3. Zone E is equipped with continuous temperature monitoring and alarms under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Any alarm, deviation outside +2 °C to +8 °C, cooling fault, door fault, sensor fault or power interruption is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. Affected stock is secured and system-blocked as not available.

4. A manual temperature verification is performed in Zone E on each shift. The morning shift and the afternoon shift each record reading, time, device identity and operator identity, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor. A missing or failed verification stops all chilled put-away, replenishment, picking and counting until a verified reading back in range is recorded.

5. Doors are opened only for active scanner tasks and closed immediately afterwards. Put-away under PR-02, replenishment to Zone C under PR-03 and cycle counts under PR-08 run without delay or intermediate staging in other zones. Exposure time outside the cold zone is kept to the minimum, and pallets not placed are returned to Zone E without delay.

6. Chilled pallets are handled only by trained inbound operators and authorised forklift operators. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Pallets exceeding this weight, unstable, overhanging, damaged, with broken cold-chain evidence, damaged insulation, or missing batch, expiry or readable labels are not stored as available stock.

7. Non-conforming chilled stock is segregated immediately and reported to the shift supervisor. Damaged, expired, suspect or cold-chain-broken goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. They are physically separated, marked, system-blocked on the handheld WMS scanner, and never picked, replenished, packed or dispatched.

8. Safe work in Zone E follows all movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving, and limits of 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramp interfaces are observed. Trucks and jacks used in Zone E are clean, dry and free of contamination.

9. Aisles, evaporators, sensors and emergency equipment in Zone E are kept fully clear. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways with yellow barriers remain unobstructed, and only assigned labelled chilled positions are used. Condensation, spillage and ice are cleaned immediately, reported, and secured where slip or contamination risk exists.

10. Every reading, alarm, deviation, quarantine transfer and open chilled task is recorded with time and operator identity and reviewed by the shift supervisor. Findings and blocks are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, confirming last verified temperature, alarm status, stock held as unavailable and pallets awaiting put-away, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Hazmat storage rules
text:
1. Hazardous packed goods are stored only in the separate ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F — services and control. The cage occupies 60 m2 inside the 600 m2 Zone F and is the only permitted location for hazmat on site. No hazmat is stored in Zones A, B, C, D or E, in transit lanes, on dock aprons or in the yard.

2. Total storage in the cage never exceeds 4,000 kg at a time under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The limit covers pallets, goods, packaging and containment combined and applies to all hazardous stock together. No put-away, replenishment or returns transfer may create or increase stock beyond this total.

3. The cage limit is built on the fixed site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg. By weight 4,000 kg divided by 800 kg equals 5 pallets, so the cage holds at most 5 full-weight pallets. Floor space does not govern: even if marked positions stand empty, the cage is closed to further receipt once 4,000 kg is reached.

4. More than 5 pallets may be held together only if their combined weight stays within 4,000 kg, which requires a correspondingly lower average weight per pallet. No hazmat pallet exceeding 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged, leaking, with broken seals, missing hazard labels or without a readable WMS label is booked, put away or stored.

5. Capacity is checked before every task is created. The forklift operator and the shift supervisor on duty confirm the current cage weight in the warehouse management system, add the planned inbound weight from Zone A, and confirm remaining capacity. No put-away task under PR-02 and PR-13 is released if the addition would exceed 4,000 kg.

6. Put-away to the cage is direct and segregated. Hazmat pallets are booked in Zone A only after document check, count and inspection, then moved directly from Zone A to the cage without staging in Zone B, C or D. Joint transport with food, drugstore, chilled or general goods on the same movement is prohibited.

7. The cage is separate, ventilated, marked and lockable, with segregation, spill containment, fire and emergency equipment kept clear and serviceable. Ventilation, seals, lighting and containment are checked as part of safe storage. Access is limited to instructed staff under the shift supervisor, and incompatible goods are never placed together to use weight reserve.

8. Every placement and removal is scan-verified by source and target on the handheld WMS scanners, with pallet identity, time and operator identity recorded. Labelling, closure, seals, leakage checks and compatibility are verified on each movement. Any leak, damaged seal, missing hazard label, vapour suspicion or cage alarm stops work and is reported immediately to the shift supervisor.

9. Safe work at the cage follows all movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving, and limits of 8 km/h inside the building and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramp interfaces are observed. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways remain unobstructed.

10. Every cage movement is reconciled against the 4,000 kg limit and reviewed by the shift supervisor. The record shows pallet identities, individual weights, total cage weight and pallets on hand, with refusals and quarantine transfers to Zone F noted. Cage weight, remaining capacity, blocks and incidents are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Spills, quarantine and damage
text:
1. Any spill, leak, damaged seal, missing hazard label, vapour suspicion or cage alarm stops work immediately under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The finder stops handling, leaves the goods where they are, secures the area against people and trucks, alerts nearby staff and reports immediately to the shift supervisor on duty.

2. The shift supervisor leads spill response and directs containment, PPE, ventilation and evacuation. Small contained leaks are contained with the cage spill equipment by instructed staff only. Spills with vapour risk, spreading liquid, fire risk or personal exposure trigger evacuation under PR-14 with assembly by the north fence and roll call before re-entry.

3. No spill is washed away, diluted, repacked or moved to drains, aisles or waste areas. Contaminated absorbents, damaged packaging and leaking units are treated as hazardous quarantine stock, marked and system-blocked as not available on the handheld WMS scanner. The cage, truck or bay stays blocked until inspected and cleared by the maintenance technician.

4. Cold-chain spills and condensation are secured under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Chilled leaks, broken insulation, damaged cold-chain evidence or temperature deviation outside +2 °C to +8 °C stop chilled movements. Affected stock is segregated, system-blocked as not available, and reported to the shift supervisor. Exposure time outside Zone E is kept to the minimum.

5. All damaged, suspect, expired and non-conforming goods go to quarantine in the marked quarantine area in Zone F the same day they are found, under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. This applies to findings in Zones A, B, C, D, E and F, during receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch, cycle counts or returns inspection. No damaged pallet waits until the next shift.

6. Quarantine is the only holding place for damaged stock. No quarantine stock is held in Zone A, Zone B bulk storage, Zone C pick faces, Zone D staging, Zone E, the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, transit lanes or the yard. Quarantined pallets are physically separated, clearly marked with cause, date, source zone and finder identity, and system-blocked as not available.

7. Blocked stock is never picked, replenished, packed, staged in Zone D, loaded or restocked until a disposition decision is recorded. Inspection of quarantined goods takes place only in Zone F by returns staff, with every unit inspected individually. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, and unstable, leaking or unreadable pallets are not stacked or racked.

8. Final disposition is restock, rework or scrap. Only intact, clean, correctly labelled and in-date units with full traceability are released back via booking to Zone B, Zone E or the cage subject to the 4,000 kg limit. Rework takes place only in value-added packing in Zone F with re-inspection. All other units remain blocked for scrap and disposal.

9. Write-off authority is fixed by a 500 EUR threshold per case. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold, and every write-off records cause, quantity, value and disposition.

10. Every spill, leak, quarantine placement, inspection result, disposition and write-off is recorded with time, pallet identity and operator identity, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor, and escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift where authority is exceeded. Open quarantine, blocks, cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit and Zone E status are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership for the incoming shift.

title: Reporting incidents
text:
1. Every incident is reported immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. This covers any damage, near miss, spill, leak, rack impact, truck or leveller fault, barrier or marking damage, temperature alarm in Zone E, hazmat leak or alarm, breach of speed, PPE or seat-belt discipline, and any personal injury. The finder stops the work concerned and reports without delay.

2. The area is secured before anything is moved. Powered trucks are stopped, lowered and secured clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and crossings where possible. Goods, pallets and equipment stay where they are, the zone is held clear of people and trucks, and no put-away, replenishment, picking or loading continues in the affected area until released.

3. Reporting runs on every shift and applies to everyone on site. This includes the morning shift 06:00-14:00, the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 and approved Saturday morning overtime, in all Zones A to F, on dock ramps at doors 1-8 and in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard. At any time during operations there is always exactly one shift supervisor in charge to receive the report.

4. The report is made in person to the shift supervisor and then recorded in writing. Each incident report records date, time, zone and door where applicable, persons and trucks involved, task and scanner reference, cause, damage, quantity and value where known, with high-visibility vest, class S3 footwear and seat-belt compliance and speed compliance at 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps noted.

5. Damaged, suspect and non-conforming goods found through an incident go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. They are physically separated, clearly marked with cause, date, source zone and finder identity, and system-blocked as not available on the handheld WMS scanner. Blocked stock is never picked, replenished, packed or dispatched until disposition is recorded.

6. The shift supervisor leads the immediate response under the relevant procedure. This is PR-09 for quarantine, PR-12 for cold-chain hold between +2 °C and +8 °C, PR-13 for hazmat spill containment in the 60 m2 cage, PR-10 and PR-11 for truck and pedestrian protection, and PR-14 for evacuation with assembly by the north fence. Instructions on safety, PPE and evacuation are binding.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report and countersigns it on the same shift. The review checks segregation, system blocking, quarantine transfer, bay or truck blocking, barrier and marking condition, and corrective action before work resumes. No affected bay, truck, lane or route is returned to service without this review and clearance.

8. Reports requiring decisions above supervisor authority are escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift. This includes any write-off above 500 EUR, any injury or structural or racking damage, bay overloads against the 2,700 kg limit, pallets above 800 kg, cage loads against the 4,000 kg limit, and any temperature deviation or spill requiring stock hold. No escalated incident is closed without warehouse manager decision.

9. Write-off discipline is fixed by the 500 EUR threshold per case. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold, and every write-off records cause, quantity, value and disposition with approval identity.

10. Every report, review, block, quarantine transfer and escalation is transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15. The outgoing shift supervisor confirms open investigations, blocked trucks and bays, quarantine quantities and cage weight, and corrective actions outstanding, with clear ownership for the incoming shift until every point is cleared.

title: Evacuation and assembly point
text:
1. Emergency evacuation is performed under PR-14 Emergency evacuation and applies to everyone on site. This includes all floor staff on the morning shift 06:00-14:00, the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 and approved Saturday morning overtime, the warehouse manager, the shift supervisor on duty, dispatchers, the maintenance technician, and any authorised visitor, contractor or driver in the 3,500 m2 fenced yard.

2. Any alarm, fire, smoke, gas suspicion, spill with vapour risk, structural damage, rack collapse or other immediate danger triggers evacuation. The person discovering the danger stops work, secures equipment where safe to do so, alerts nearby staff, activates the nearest alarm call point and reports immediately to the shift supervisor on duty.

3. On alarm all receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, loading, counting and maintenance stop at once. Powered trucks are stopped, forks lowered and secured clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, crossings and dock ramps where possible. Dock levellers at the 1.2 m doors are left in place and exits are not blocked with pallets, jacks or wrappers.

4. Everyone leaves the 6,000 m2 hall immediately on foot by the marked escape routes. Only the 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways, marked crossings and signed exits are used, moving away from the danger to the outside. Trucks, hand pallet jacks, lifts and personal belongings are not used or collected, and running, overtaking and re-entry for goods are prohibited.

5. Drivers in the marked waiting area do not enter the hall and do not move vehicles. On alarm they leave trucks where safely parked, switch off where required, move on foot by the marked pedestrian routes to the assembly point and follow dispatcher and shift supervisor instructions. No vehicle enters, leaves or reverses in the yard during evacuation.

6. The assembly point is the marked area by the north fence outside the hall. All evacuated persons assemble there by shift, zone and role, clear of dock aprons at doors 1-8, manoeuvring areas and access routes for emergency services. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain worn, and the area is kept clear of pallets and equipment.

7. Roll call is performed at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor on duty conducts the roll call against the shift attendance, the PR-15 handover record, the visitor log and the dispatcher driver list. Missing, injured or unaccounted persons are reported immediately to emergency services and the warehouse manager.

8. No one re-enters the hall, yard work areas, dock ramps or Zones A to F until the roll call is complete and re-entry is explicitly authorised. The shift supervisor secures the building against re-entry and releases it only after clearance by emergency services or, for drills and false alarms, by the shift supervisor with the warehouse manager informed. Partial or individual re-entry is prohibited.

9. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. Each drill covers alarm activation, stopping of work and securing of trucks, escape by marked routes, yard and driver control, assembly by the north fence and roll call before authorised re-entry. Timing is rotated across mornings, afternoons and, where applicable, Saturday overtime so all 38 to 40 staff practise.

10. Every alarm, evacuation, drill, missing person and re-entry authorisation is recorded with date, time, zones and doors involved, attendance count, findings and corrective actions, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor. Barrier, marking, alarm and exit faults are logged for the maintenance technician and block the route until repaired. Records are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15.

title: Inspections, drills and follow-up
text:
1. Scheduled safety checks and drills run on fixed routines under PR-08, PR-10, PR-12, PR-13 and PR-14. They apply on the morning shift 06:00-14:00, the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00 and approved Saturday morning overtime. No routine is skipped for workload, delay or shift targets, and the shift supervisor on duty enforces completion.

2. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10. The authorised operator assigned to the truck checks brakes, steering, horn, lights, mirrors, seat belt, forks and carriage, chains, wheels and tyres, battery charge and cables, hydraulics, emergency stop and rating plate. For the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t reach, tilt and height functions are included, and for the 8 electric pallet jacks tiller, drive and lift controls.

3. A truck with any safety fault is blocked immediately, tagged as not for use and parked clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, crossings and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways. The operator reports to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician. The 6 counterbalance trucks rated at 2.5 t, reach trucks and electric jacks return to service only after repair logged and cleared by the maintenance technician.

4. Racking is subject to documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects uprights, beams, beam locks, bracing, floor fixings and labels across Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C flow racks and Zone E positions, and records date, area, findings and signature. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg and block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m, built on a pallet of at most 800 kg.

5. Any impact, deformation, cracked upright, loose beam, missing lock, overload evidence or falling material blocks the bay immediately. The bay is unloaded if required and secured against put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03 and picking under PR-04 until cleared. The finding is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, recorded as an incident and logged for repair.

6. Zone E of 300 m2 is held between +2 °C and +8 °C with continuous monitoring and alarms under PR-12. A manual temperature verification is performed on each shift with reading, time, device identity and operator identity recorded and countersigned by the shift supervisor. A missing or failed verification or any alarm stops all chilled movements, blocks affected stock as not available and holds exposure time to the minimum.

7. The 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F is checked against the 4,000 kg limit, at most 5 full-weight pallets, on every placement and removal under PR-13. Labelling, closure, seals, leakage, compatibility, ventilation, spill containment and fire equipment are verified on each movement. Any leak, damaged seal, missing hazard label, vapour suspicion or cage alarm stops work, blocks the cage, truck or bay and triggers spill response.

8. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. Each drill covers alarm activation, stopping of work and securing of trucks, escape on foot by marked routes, yard and driver control in the 3,500 m2 yard, assembly at the marked area by the north fence and roll call before authorised re-entry. Timing rotates across mornings, afternoons and Saturday overtime so all 38 to 40 staff practise.

9. Barriers, markings, alarms and exits are checked as part of every inspection and drill and after every incident. The 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, 4.0 m and 3.0 m aisles, mirrors, signs, dock levellers at the 1.2 m doors, spill and fire equipment are kept clear and serviceable. Any defect blocks the route or equipment until repaired and logged. High-visibility vests, class S3 footwear and seat belts whenever moving remain mandatory.

10. Every check, inspection, repair, drill, alarm, block and corrective action is recorded with date, time, identities and findings, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor and escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift where authority is exceeded, including write-offs above 500 EUR. Open blocks, quarantine in Zone F, cage weight, Zone E status and enforcement action are transferred in the documented end-of-shift handover at 14:00 and 22:00 under PR-15, with clear ownership until cleared.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. This covers all operations from receiving at doors 1-4 through Zone B, C, E and F to dispatch at doors 5-8, occupational safety, inventory accuracy, and all final sign-offs. This accountability cannot be delegated to shift supervisors, dispatchers or other staff.

2. The warehouse manager leads the site organisation of around 38 to 40 people across the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only. The 2 shift supervisors, 2 dispatchers, stock controllers and maintenance technician report directly to the warehouse manager on operations, safety and stock matters.

3. The warehouse manager sets the shift plan, defines zone discipline for Zones A to F, and owns the system of fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15 as a whole. The manager approves any new version of a procedure and is the only person who can approve a temporary departure from a procedure, and only with a documented instruction and compensating safety measure.

4. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime. No extension of the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts, no Saturday morning working, and no work outside operating hours takes place without prior written approval from the warehouse manager. Shift supervisors and dispatchers cannot authorise overtime.

5. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators. No employee operates the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t or the 8 electric pallet jacks without this prior personal authorisation, recorded by name, truck type and date. No licence, no truck.

6. The warehouse manager signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results. The stocktake is prepared by the 2 stock controllers on the basis of full counts, second counts and recounts across all 2,400 positions in Zone B, Zone C, Zone E and Zone F, but the result becomes binding only with the manager signature. No adjustment from the stocktake is posted without this sign-off.

7. Write-off authority above 500 EUR belongs exclusively to the warehouse manager. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case; any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold, and every write-off records cause, quantity, value and disposition.

8. The warehouse manager is the escalation point for every matter that exceeds supervisor or dispatcher authority. This includes injuries, structural and racking damage, bay overloads against the 2,700 kg limit, pallets above the 800 kg site standard, cage loads against the 4,000 kg limit, temperature deviations outside +2 °C to +8 °C, and unresolved incident reports. No escalated incident is closed without manager decision.

9. The warehouse manager ensures readiness of the all-electric fleet, the 8 levellers at 1.2 m dock height, the 2 stretch wrappers, cardboard baler and 20 WMS scanners, the monthly documented racking inspection, quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence, and manual temperature verification each shift. Faults affecting safety or load capacity are cleared through the maintenance log.

10. The warehouse manager controls performance through the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00, the dispatcher booking lists for doors 1-4 inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only, and review of incident reports, cycle counts, quarantine in Zone F and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. Work restarts only on accepted handover with clear ownership, with high-visibility vest, class S3 footwear and seat-belt discipline enforced throughout.

title: Shift Supervisors
text:
1. The 2 shift supervisors run the floor at Harborwick 3PL Ltd., one on the morning shift from 06:00 to 14:00 and one on the afternoon shift from 14:00 to 22:00. At any time during operating hours there is always exactly one shift supervisor in charge of the floor, and instructions from the supervisor on duty are binding for all floor staff.

2. The shift supervisor on duty directs all floor staff during the shift: forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, maintenance technician support, dispatch interface and the 2 floaters covering absence. The supervisor allocates tasks within the shift plan set by the warehouse manager, ensures labour, scanners and equipment cover at doors 1-4 inbound and doors 5-8 outbound, and enforces zone discipline for Zones A to F.

3. The shift supervisor enforces the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15 on the floor. No receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch, counting or maintenance task runs outside its procedure. If a procedure cannot be followed, the supervisor stops the work concerned, secures goods and equipment where they are, records the deviation as an incident and escalates to the warehouse manager.

4. The shift supervisor verifies safety readiness before allocating work. No scanner task is assigned to an unauthorised operator or to an unchecked or blocked truck, no work starts without high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear, and seat belts whenever the truck is moving are enforced. Speeds of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are enforced, and speeding, barrier breaches and aisle blocking are stopped immediately.

5. The shift supervisor ensures readiness of Zone A for each booked arrival, Zone C faces replenished before each picking shift, and Zone D staged by door and load for release. The supervisor does not change dispatcher door assignments for doors 1-4 inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only without agreement from the dispatcher, and no truck is loaded, unloaded or sealed without dispatcher release under PR-06.

6. The shift supervisor leads immediate response to any incident, damage, near miss, spill, rack impact, truck or leveller fault, temperature alarm in Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C, hazmat leak in the 60 m2 cage, or personal injury. The supervisor secures the area, directs response under PR-09, PR-12, PR-13 or PR-14, orders quarantine in Zone F the same day damage is found, and blocks the bay, truck, lane or route until cleared.

7. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report and countersigns it on the same shift. Each review checks segregation, system blocking on the handheld WMS scanners, quarantine transfer, bay or truck blocking, PPE and speed compliance, and corrective action before work resumes. Reports requiring decisions above supervisor authority are escalated to the warehouse manager the same shift.

8. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case. Any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved for the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold, and every write-off is documented with cause, quantity, value, location or delivery reference and approval identity.

9. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of all inspected returns. Returns staff in Zone F inspect every unit within the 14-day acceptance rule and propose restock, rework or scrap, but no restock to Zone B, E or the cage subject to the 4,000 kg limit, no rework and no scrap takes place without this recorded approval under PR-07 and PR-09.

10. The shift supervisor performs the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00, and for approved Saturday morning overtime on the same discipline. The outgoing and incoming supervisors sign the record with date, time and identities, confirming dock bookings, open loads, replenishment, cycle counts, quarantine, cage weight, Zone E verification, blocks and incidents. The supervisor cannot approve overtime and cannot authorise new forklift operators, and work restarts only on accepted handover with clear ownership.

title: Dispatchers
text:
1. The 2 dispatchers control transport and dock doors at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. across the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only. They report to the warehouse manager on operations and work shift by shift with the shift supervisor on duty on the floor.

2. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling for the whole site. This covers booking of all inbound, outbound, van and returns transport, fixing the sequence of arrivals and departures per shift, and balancing doors 1-4 inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only against capacity in Zone A receiving and Zone D dispatch. No other role changes a booking or door assignment.

3. Every carrier is assigned a specific door and a fixed time slot by the dispatcher before arrival. No truck arrives unannounced, no truck chooses its own door, and no inbound truck is directed to outbound doors 5-8 and no outbound truck to inbound doors 1-4. Early, late, double-booked or unbooked arrivals are held for revised dispatcher instruction.

4. The dispatcher manages the fenced yard of 3,500 m2 through assignment only. Drivers report at the yard entrance with booking reference, move only to the marked waiting area and wait there until called to the 1.2 m door with its own leveller. Drivers never enter the hall, Zone A, Zone D or Zone F and take no part in unloading, loading, counting, wrapping or sealing.

5. The dispatcher calls trucks to the door only when the door, Zone A lanes or Zone D staging and labour are ready. Reversing, leveller placing by trained warehouse staff, securing of the vehicle and document handover at the cab or door interface run on dispatcher sequence. No truck moves to a door, docks or pulls off without dispatcher instruction.

6. The dispatcher defines staging and loading order in the 900 m2 Zone D under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Pallets are staged only as wrapped, labelled and scanner-confirmed pallets in marked door lanes by door, load and time slot. The dispatcher confirms that planned trailer totals respect 22,000 kg and 33 positions, van totals respect 1,200 kg and 6 positions, and shift totals respect the 324 full-weight pallet promise limit.

7. The dispatcher owns outbound load release. No truck is loaded or sealed without prior recorded dispatcher release confirming complete load, wrapped and labelled pallets with readable system labels, matching carrier, door from doors 5-8 and time slot. After loading, count reconciliation, sealing with recorded seal number and recorded departure run only on dispatcher instruction.

8. The dispatcher coordinates returns and exceptions through rebooking. Returns within 14 days of delivery arrive only on dispatcher booking for receipt at doors 1-4 and transfer to Zone F. Time-slot deviations, door changes, waiting times, leveller faults and open loads are recorded by door and delivery, clarified with carrier or client, and passed to the shift supervisor for Zone A readiness or Zone D correction.

9. The dispatcher does not hold authorities reserved to others. The dispatcher does not approve overtime, does not authorise new forklift operators, does not approve damaged-goods write-offs, and does not approve final disposition of inspected returns. Matters above dispatcher authority, including write-offs above 500 EUR and procedure departures, are escalated via the shift supervisor to the warehouse manager.

10. The dispatcher provides the booking and release record for the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00, and for approved Saturday morning overtime on the same discipline. The record confirms bookings by door and time slot, carriers at doors 1-8, trucks still in the waiting area, loads released, loaded, sealed or pending correction, and rebooked slots. No open truck or load is carried silently, and work restarts only on accepted handover with clear ownership.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. The 6 inbound operators staff Zone A — receiving of 800 m2 at inbound doors 1-4. They work on the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty and to the dispatcher door and time-slot assignment.

2. The inbound operators own the Zone A document check as the mandatory first step under PR-01 Inbound receiving. They verify booking reference, client and order, pallet and carton quantities, product identities, batch or expiry data, and cold-chain or hazmat papers where applicable. No goods are unloaded before this check is recorded as passed for that truck and door.

3. If documents are missing, incomplete or do not match the booking, the inbound operator stops the receipt, holds goods and vehicle at the door, keeps the area clear and informs the shift supervisor and dispatcher immediately. No unloading, counting or booking starts until the decision to hold, partially receive or refuse is recorded.

4. After document release the inbound operators unload, count and inspect with trained forklift operators in support. They use hand pallet jacks and, where instructed, electric pallet jacks, place pallets only in marked Zone A lanes, and keep 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways clear. The leveller at the 1.2 m door is operated only by trained warehouse staff, never by the driver.

5. Every delivery is counted pallet by pallet and, where required, carton by carton against the checked documents, confirmed on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners. Shortages, overages, mislabelled pallets and unreadable labels are segregated in Zone A, marked as pending and reported to the shift supervisor before any booking.

6. Every delivery is inspected in Zone A before booking under PR-01. Packaging integrity, pallet condition, labelling, visible damage, contamination and expiry or temperature indicators are checked. Chilled goods are checked for cold-chain evidence under PR-12 and hazmat for labelling, closure and leakage under PR-13, with deviations reported immediately.

7. Only goods that have passed document check, count and inspection are released for system booking and put-away. The inbound operator scans each released pallet, confirms client, product, quantity, batch or storage requirement, and records door from doors 1-4, delivery reference, time and identity. Uncounted, uninspected, damaged or quarantined goods are never booked as available stock.

8. The inbound operators enforce Zone A discipline and limits. Nothing moves past Zone A to Zone B, E or F without release, and no pallet exceeding 800 kg including load, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label is booked for put-away. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods are marked, segregated and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

9. The inbound operators work to full movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, seat belts are fastened whenever a truck is moving, and limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are observed. Drivers are kept in the marked waiting area in the 3,500 m2 yard and never enter Zone A or take part in handling.

10. The inbound operators clear Zone A by delivery for the next booked carrier and hand over all open work under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. They confirm which loads are booked, released and awaiting put-away to Zone B with 2,400 positions, Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C or the 60 m2 cage subject to 4,000 kg, and which deliveries remain held. They do not approve overtime, authorise forklift operators or approve write-offs, and escalate all exceptions to the shift supervisor.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. The 8 forklift operators carry out all powered handling at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. They work on the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty and only on active WMS scanner tasks.

2. No licence, no truck. Forklift operators drive only with prior personal authorisation from the warehouse manager, recorded by name, truck type and date. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks are never driven without this authorisation, and no other role operates forklifts, reach trucks or electric pallet jacks.

3. Authorisation is type-specific and task-bound. General work across Zone A, the 4.0 m main transport aisles and Zone D runs on counterbalance trucks, high-bay work in the 3.0 m rack aisles of Zone B with 2,400 positions runs on reach trucks, and horizontal and dock work runs on electric pallet jacks. An operator authorised for one type does not drive another type.

4. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. The assigned operator checks brakes, steering, horn, lights, mirrors, seat belt, forks and carriage, chains, wheels and tyres, battery charge and cables, hydraulics, emergency stop and rating plate, plus reach, tilt and height on reach trucks and tiller, drive and lift on electric jacks, with identity, date and time recorded.

5. A truck with any safety fault is blocked immediately. The operator tags it as not for use, parks it clear of 4.0 m aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, crossings and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways, and reports to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician. A blocked truck returns to service only after repair logged and cleared by the maintenance technician.

6. Forklift operators perform put-away under PR-02, replenishment of Zone C faces under PR-03, staging to the 900 m2 Zone D, and loading and unloading at the 1.2 m dock doors. They scan-verify source and target on the 20 shared handheld scanners, keep transport and pedestrian routes clear, and never move pallets from Zone A without release or load a truck without dispatcher release under PR-06.

7. Load limits are fixed and never exceeded. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg, each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. Only stable, fully supported pallets with readable labels are lifted. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, damaged or unreadable pallets are refused, segregated and reported.

8. Movement and PPE discipline applies to every move. Seat belts are fastened whenever the truck is moving, high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, and limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps are observed. Pedestrians have priority, and horn, lights and mirrors are used at every junction.

9. Forklift operators respect zone and goods discipline. Standard goods go to Zone B, chilled goods directly to Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C without staging elsewhere, and hazmat directly to the 60 m2 ventilated cage subject to 4,000 kg without staging in Zone B, C or D. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Levellers, the 2 stretch wrappers and scanners are used only where trained.

10. Forklift operators hand over all open work under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. They confirm tasks completed and uncompleted, blocked trucks and bays, overweight or damaged pallets, and any impact, near miss or fault for stock controller and maintenance follow-up. They do not approve overtime, authorise operators or approve write-offs, and escalate all exceptions to the shift supervisor.

title: Pickers
text:
1. The 10 pickers pick customer orders in Zone C — picking of 1,200 m2. They work on the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty and only against active WMS scanner tasks.

2. Picking takes place only in Zone C and only after the assigned faces have been replenished and released for the shift under PR-03. No picking takes place in Zone A, B, D, E or F, and no picker picks from reserve stock, quarantine, returns pending inspection or the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage.

3. The pickers work on ground-level pick faces and flow-rack front aisles using the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners. Each picker logs on with personal identity, accepts one task at a time under PR-04 Order picking, and follows the scanner sequence by location, product, quantity and batch or expiry where applicable.

4. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. The picker scans the face or lane label, then scans each item or carton label, and confirms quantity on the scanner. Mismatched product, wrong batch, over-pick and short-pick are blocked by the system, and unscanned or manually counted items are never forwarded.

5. First-in, first-out rotation is mandatory. Flow racks are picked only from the front picking side in lane order, ground faces are picked from the indicated stock, and only the batch directed by the scanner is picked. Expired, damaged, mislabelled or unreadable stock is not picked but segregated and reported.

6. Pick faces are never over-picked or forcibly emptied. If the tasked quantity is not available, the face is empty, the label is missing or the scanner flags zero stock, the picker stops that line, records the short pick on the scanner, leaves the lane clear, and informs the shift supervisor and stock controllers for second count.

7. Picked goods are placed only in designated picking carts, totes or pallets for that order, by order and line. Mixed orders, mixed batches and loose stacking are prohibited. Stability and weight distribution are observed on every build on the site standard of a pallet, load included, of at most 800 kg.

8. The pickers keep Zone C clear and ordered during picking. Film, cardboard and packaging waste is removed to the 1 cardboard baler, spillages and condensation are cleaned and reported immediately, and front picking aisles, crossings and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways are kept clear. Main aisles of 4.0 m and rack aisles of 3.0 m are never blocked.

9. The pickers work to full movement and PPE discipline on foot. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, only walkways and marked crossings are used, and pedestrians have priority with eye contact and waiting until trucks stop. Powered replenishment trucks observe 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and Zone C interfaces. Pickers use hand pallet jacks at walking pace and never drive forklifts, reach trucks or electric pallet jacks.

10. The pickers close completed picks line by line on the scanner with location, quantity, time and identity and hand scan-verified picks for packing, labelling and transfer to Zone D under PR-05. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09, and open orders, short picks and blocked faces are handed over under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. They do not approve overtime, authorise operators or approve write-offs, and escalate all exceptions to the shift supervisor.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. The 4 returns and packing staff work in Zone F — services and control of 600 m2 and in packing. They work on the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty.

2. In Zone F they own returns inspection under PR-07 Returns handling. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery, arrive only on dispatcher booking at doors 1-4 and are moved promptly to the marked returns inspection area. Every returned unit is system-blocked as not available and inspected individually, without sampling.

3. Inspection covers packaging integrity, sealing, labelling, batch and expiry data, contamination, damage and signs of use or tampering, with cold-chain evidence checked under PR-12 and hazard labelling and closure checked under PR-13. Uninspected, unscanned or manually estimated units are never forwarded for decision.

4. For every inspected unit the returns and packing staff propose the disposition: restock to available stock, rework in value-added packing, or scrap. Only intact, clean, correctly labelled and in-date units with full traceability are proposed for restock; repairable outer faults are proposed for rework; damaged, expired, tampered or non-conforming units are proposed for scrap.

5. No restock, rework or scrap takes place without recorded approval of the final disposition by the shift supervisor. Approved restock is booked via the system only to Zone B with 2,400 positions, Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C or the 60 m2 ventilated cage subject to 4,000 kg, never directly to Zone C faces or Zone D staging.

6. In packing the staff perform packing and labelling under PR-05. They accept only scan-verified picks closed on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, pack by order, line, client and delivery with batch separation where directed, and never forward unscanned, partially picked or suspect goods to Zone D.

7. Every outbound pallet and carton carries a readable system label checked against the scanner task for client, product, quantity, destination and door. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, damaged or mislabelled pallets are segregated and reported, and damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

8. The staff operate the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and the 1 cardboard baler only where instructed. Pallets are wrapped to a stable, transport-safe standard without obscuring labels, unstable wraps are re-wrapped, and cardboard, film and packaging waste is removed continuously so 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m barrier-separated walkways stay clear.

9. The staff work to full movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, limits of 8 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are observed, and only walkways and marked crossings are used on foot. Hand pallet jacks are used at walking pace; forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks are never driven.

10. The staff record every receipt, inspection result, proposal, packing confirmation and quarantine transfer with time and identity and hand over all open work under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. They confirm units awaiting disposition approval, rework in progress, scrap awaiting disposal and write-offs within the 500 EUR authority rule. They do not approve overtime, authorise forklift operators or approve write-offs, and escalate all exceptions to the shift supervisor.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. The 2 stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. They work on the Monday to Friday two-shift system, mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty for daily execution and reporting to the warehouse manager on stock matters.

2. The stock in the system is the stock on the rack. The stock controllers ensure that every pallet in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone between +2 °C and +8 °C, and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage and quarantine in Zone F has one recorded location in the warehouse management system. No pallet exists without a system location.

3. The stock controllers run the daily cycle counts under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. Counts run every working day on a rotating zone schedule so all locations are covered in rotation. The controllers define the daily rotation, release count tasks on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners, and direct counters by zone, bay, face or cage position.

4. Counting runs only against active scanner tasks with personal identity. The controllers require scan of the location label then scan of each pallet and carton label, with quantity, product, batch or expiry confirmed on the scanner. Manual estimates, unscanned quantities and counts from memory are prohibited and rejected.

5. Only inspected and booked stock is counted as available. Quarantine in Zone F, returns pending inspection, hazmat stock against the 4,000 kg limit and any pallet held in Zone A awaiting booking are counted separately as blocked or unavailable. Empty faces, zero-stock flags and double occupations are confirmed on the scanner.

6. Every count is reconciled immediately against the system. Matches are closed with location, quantity, time and counter identity. Any difference stops closure for that location, the location is physically secured and marked for recount, and the shift supervisor is informed before any put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03 or picking under PR-04 continues there.

7. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. A different counter from the first count recounts the secured location independently, re-scans all labels and confirms unit of measure, batch and expiry. Only a confirmed difference is prepared as an adjustment with cause, quantity, value and both counter identities. Unconfirmed differences are recounted again.

8. The stock controllers prepare adjustments but do not approve write-offs. Damaged goods found during counting go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Write-offs follow the fixed 500 EUR threshold, with the shift supervisor approving up to and including 500 EUR and the warehouse manager approving above 500 EUR, and stocktake discrepancies are escalated the same shift.

9. The stock controllers prepare and lead the annual wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08. They freeze system stock, define the count sequence, release stocktake scanner tasks, assign independent count teams and control recounts and adjustment preparation across Zone B, Zone C, Zone E and Zone F. The result becomes binding only with the signature of the warehouse manager.

10. The stock controllers record every count, second count, pending recount and prepared adjustment and hand over all open work under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. They confirm zones counted, locations blocked for recount, adjustments awaiting approval, quarantine transfers and rack damage for the maintenance technician. They do not approve overtime, authorise forklift operators or approve write-offs, and escalate all exceptions to the shift supervisor and warehouse manager, working in high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear with limits of 8 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps observed.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. The maintenance technician maintains all trucks, racking and dock equipment at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. The technician works Monday to Friday, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only, under the direction of the shift supervisor on duty for daily priorities and reporting to the warehouse manager on condition, safety and load capacity.

2. The technician owns the condition of the all-electric fleet: 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. The technician also maintains chargers, batteries and cables, the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, the 1 cardboard baler, the 8 levellers at the 1.2 m dock doors and the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners.

3. The technician supports the documented check of every powered truck before its first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Check forms, rating plates, seat belts, brakes, steering, horn, lights, mirrors, forks, chains, hydraulics and emergency stops are kept serviceable, and any truck with a safety fault stays blocked, tagged as not for use, until inspected, repaired and logged as cleared.

4. The technician performs the documented safety inspection of racking every month. All high-bay racking in Zone B with 2,400 positions, flow racks in Zone C, and positions in Zone E are inspected for uprights, beams, beam locks, bracing, floor fixings and bay labels, with date, area, findings and signature recorded. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg and block-stacking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m.

5. Any impact, deformation, cracked upright, loose beam, missing lock, overload evidence or falling material blocks the bay immediately. The technician unloads the bay if required, secures it against put-away under PR-02, replenishment under PR-03 and picking under PR-04, and clears it for reuse only after repair. The finding is treated as an incident reviewed by the shift supervisor.

6. The technician maintains dock, building and safety equipment: levellers at doors 1-4 inbound only and doors 5-8 outbound only, doors, barriers, yellow barriers on the 1.2 m walkways, floor markings, signs, mirrors, lighting, cooling units, seals and sensors in Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C, and ventilation, segregation, spill containment, fire and emergency equipment at the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage subject to 4,000 kg.

7. Every repair is logged by the technician. The log records truck identity or bay and equipment reference, fault description, date and time found, person reporting, repair performed, parts used and clearance for reuse. Faults affecting safety or load capacity block the truck, bay, lane or route, and no instruction, delay or shift target overrides the block.

8. The technician acts immediately on alarms and faults reported by the shift supervisor: temperature alarms and cooling, door or sensor faults in Zone E under PR-12, leaks, seal damage, vapour suspicion or cage alarms under PR-13, and barrier, marking, alarm and exit faults found in quarterly evacuation drills under PR-14 with assembly by the north fence. The cage, truck or bay stays blocked until cleared.

9. The technician works to full movement and PPE discipline. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory, seat belts are fastened whenever a truck is moved for test, and limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and ramps are observed. Main aisles of 4.0 m, rack aisles of 3.0 m and walkways are kept clear during all maintenance.

10. The technician records all inspections, repairs, blocks and clearances and hands over open work under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. The handover confirms trucks in service or blocked, bays blocked, leveller, wrapper and scanner faults, Zone E and cage equipment status, and corrective actions outstanding for the incoming shift. The technician does not approve overtime, authorise new forklift operators or approve write-offs, and escalates all exceptions to the shift supervisor and warehouse manager.

title: Common Rules and Training
text:
1. All roles at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. work within one common organisation of around 38 to 40 people. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site for operations, safety and final sign-offs. The 2 shift supervisors, 2 dispatchers, 2 stock controllers and maintenance technician report directly to the warehouse manager, and all floor staff work under the shift supervisor on duty.

2. Each shift has exactly one shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The morning shift runs from 06:00 to 14:00 and the afternoon shift from 14:00 to 22:00, Monday to Friday, with Saturday morning overtime in peak season only. Instructions from the supervisor on duty on safety, PPE, zone stops and evacuation are binding for every role.

3. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime, authorises new forklift operators and approves temporary departures from procedure. Only the warehouse manager signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake and write-offs above 500 EUR. Shift supervisors approve write-offs up to 500 EUR and final disposition of inspected returns. Dispatchers own dock scheduling and outbound release.

4. Every person on the warehouse floor wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear at all times, with no exceptions. Vests are worn closed and visible, footwear is worn correctly laced and serviceable. Any person without correct PPE leaves the floor immediately and reports to the shift supervisor, and work does not start or continue without full PPE.

5. Forklift operators and drivers of any powered truck wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. The belt is fastened before moving off and remains fastened until the truck is fully stopped and secured. Trucks with defective belts are blocked, tagged as not for use and reported to the shift supervisor and maintenance technician.

6. No licence, no truck applies to every role. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and the 8 electric pallet jacks are driven only by operators personally authorised by the warehouse manager, recorded by name, truck type and date. No other role operates forklifts, reach trucks or electric pallet jacks. The 12 hand pallet jacks are used on foot at walking pace by instructed staff.

7. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10. Only authorised operators perform the check, and only checked trucks receive scanner tasks. Speed limits of 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the 3,500 m2 yard and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps apply to all moves, with pedestrians having priority.

8. Mandatory training starts on day one for every starter before any unsupervised work. Zone discipline for Zones A to F, PPE, pedestrian use of the 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, speed limits, alarm and evacuation routes to the north fence assembly point, and the rule that damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day are trained and confirmed.

9. Role training follows the fifteen written procedures PR-01 to PR-15 and is completed before the task is performed alone. Inbound operators train under PR-01, forklift operators under PR-02, PR-03, PR-06 and PR-10, pickers under PR-04, packing and returns staff under PR-05, PR-07 and PR-09, stock controllers under PR-08, and all roles under PR-11, PR-14 and PR-15. Floaters are trained for the role they cover and follow its procedure.

10. Common discipline closes every shift under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00. Every incident is reported immediately to the shift supervisor, every quarantine transfer, second count, cage movement against the 4,000 kg limit and Zone E verification between +2 °C and +8 °C is recorded, and no pallet above 800 kg, no bay above 2,700 kg and no adjustment without a second count is accepted. Work restarts only on documented handover with clear ownership.

title: Receiving Slots and Intake
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides inbound receiving at doors 1-4, inbound only, within the Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. All inbound trucks arrive only on a prior booking confirmed by the dispatcher, with a specific door and fixed time slot. No unbooked receiving is promised.

2. The dispatcher owns slot allocation and balances bookings against Zone A capacity of 800 m2. The Client submits inbound notifications with booking reference, quantities, product identities and batch or expiry data in time for slot confirmation. Early, late or unannounced arrivals wait for a revised dispatcher instruction and are not handled outside sequence.

3. Each booked slot covers one trailer or van at one door at 1.2 m dock height with leveller. Drivers report at the yard entrance, wait only in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard, and never enter the hall or Zone A. Drivers take no part in unloading, counting or inspection.

4. Unloading starts only after the document check under PR-01 has been recorded as passed for that truck and door. Inbound operators verify delivery note, Client and order reference, pallet and carton quantities, product identities and, where applicable, cold-chain or hazmat papers against the dispatcher booking. Missing or mismatched documents stop unloading until the dispatcher clarifies hold, partial receipt or refusal with the Client or carrier.

5. After document release, Harborwick unloads, counts and inspects in Zone A. Every delivery is counted pallet by pallet and, where required, carton by carton on WMS scanners. Packaging, pallet condition, labelling, visible damage, contamination and expiry or temperature indicators are inspected. Nothing moves past Zone A until count and inspection are complete.

6. Only goods that have passed document check, count and inspection are booked into the warehouse management system as available stock and released to put-away to Zone B, Zone E or the Zone F cage. Uncounted, uninspected, damaged or non-conforming goods are never booked as available. They are segregated in Zone A and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

7. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Pallets exceeding 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label are not booked or put away. Harborwick holds such pallets as pending in Zone A, reports the exception to the Client, and refuses or quarantines as instructed and recorded.

8. Chilled goods are checked for cold-chain evidence and moved directly to Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C without intermediate staging. Hazmat is checked for labelling, closure and leakage and moved directly to the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F subject to the 4,000 kg limit. Standard goods exceeding cage, cold-zone or bulk capacity are held in Zone A for rebooking or refusal.

9. Zone A is cleared by delivery for the next booked carrier. Booked pallets are released promptly for put-away, quarantine transfers are completed the same day, and shortages, overages, damages and pending holds are recorded by door, delivery and pallet and reported to the Client with the inbound confirmation.

10. Additional intake outside shift hours, including Saturday morning overtime in peak season, is provided only as pre-agreed overtime approved in writing by the warehouse manager. There is no regular night, Saturday afternoon or Sunday receiving. Open inbound loads and rebooked slots at 14:00 and 22:00 are carried with clear ownership under PR-15 until booked or resolved.

title: Dispatch Capacity and Release
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides outbound dispatch at doors 5-8, outbound only, within the Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. All outbound loads run only on a prior booking confirmed by the dispatcher, with a specific door, fixed time slot and released load. No unbooked loading is promised.

2. Outbound door capacity is fixed at 3 trailer loads per door per shift across 4 doors. This equals 12 trailer loads per shift in total. The dispatcher sequences doors 5-8 against Zone D staging capacity of 900 m2, wrapper output and scanner-confirmed labour, and no truck moves to a door without dispatcher call from the marked waiting area.

3. Each trailer is a contracted curtain-side trailer rated at 22,000 kg payload on 33 floor positions. Both limits apply together. For full-weight pallets of 800 kg including load, the weight limit governs: 22,000 kg divided by 800 kg equals 27.5 pallets, so at most 27 pallets. Harborwick therefore promises at most 27 full-weight pallets per trailer.

4. The maximum dispatch promise per shift is 324 full-weight pallets. Four doors multiplied by 3 loads equals 12 loads, multiplied by 27 pallets equals 324 pallets. This is a promise limit, not a staging target. Bookings exceeding 324 full-weight equivalents per shift are split across shifts before staging in Zone D.

5. The site delivery van is rated at 1,200 kg on 6 positions. Both limits apply together. For full-weight pallets the van takes at most one pallet of 800 kg. The allocation rule is fixed: single-pallet consignments up to 1,200 kg total go by van, and anything heavier goes by trailer. Six pallets together require an average of no more than 200 kg per pallet.

6. Harborwick stages only packed, labelled and wrapped pallets in Zone D. Every pallet is scan-verified on WMS scanners for Client, order, product, quantity, destination and door, carries a readable system label, and is wrapped on the semi-automatic stretch wrappers to a stable, transport-safe standard. Unwrapped, unlabelled or scan-unconfirmed goods are never staged or loaded.

7. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, damaged, unwrapped or mislabelled pallets are not loaded. Harborwick segregates such pallets in Zone D, reports the exception to the Client, and moves damaged goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

8. No truck is loaded without prior recorded dispatcher release under PR-06. Release confirms complete load, wrapped and labelled pallets, matching carrier, door from doors 5-8 and time slot, and trailer totals within 22,000 kg and 33 positions or van totals within 1,200 kg and 6 positions. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area, never enter Zone D, and take no part in staging, loading or sealing.

9. Loading is performed only by authorised forklift operators with scan-verification pallet by pallet against the release at the 1.2 m door with leveller. After loading the count is reconciled against release and transport documents. An incomplete or disputed load is not sealed. Sealing runs only on dispatcher instruction, with seal number recorded against delivery, door, carrier and time.

10. Additional dispatch outside shift hours, including Saturday morning overtime in peak season, is provided only as pre-agreed overtime approved in writing by the warehouse manager. There is no regular night, Saturday afternoon or Sunday dispatch. Open loads, staged pallets and rebooked slots at 14:00 and 22:00 are carried with clear ownership under PR-15 and reported to the Client with the outbound confirmation.

title: Operating Hours and Cut-offs
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates Monday to Friday on two fixed shifts: mornings 06:00-14:00 and afternoons 14:00-22:00. All regular inbound receiving at doors 1-4, storage, picking, packing and outbound dispatch at doors 5-8 take place within these shifts. Outside these hours the hall is closed and secured and no handling, loading or unloading is promised.

2. There is no regular night operation and no regular weekend operation. In peak season additional capacity is provided only as Saturday morning overtime, planned in advance for backlog clearance, replenishment and outbound preparation. There is no regular Saturday afternoon, Saturday night or Sunday working.

3. Any work outside the Monday to Friday shifts, including Saturday morning overtime, is provided only as pre-agreed overtime approved in writing by the warehouse manager. Shift supervisors, dispatchers and other staff cannot authorise overtime. Without this approval no intake, staging, loading or release is promised outside shift hours.

4. Each shift is run by one designated shift supervisor in charge of the floor, with continuous supervision between 06:00 and 22:00 on working days. Continuity at 14:00 and 22:00 is maintained by documented handover under PR-15. Open inbound loads, staged pallets in Zone D, rebooked slots and pending exceptions are carried with clear ownership and reported in the shift confirmations to the Client.

5. Throughput per shift is limited by fixed door and vehicle capacities. Four outbound doors 5-8 each handle 3 trailer loads per shift, totalling 12 trailer loads per shift. Four inbound doors 1-4 are balanced by the dispatcher against Zone A capacity of 800 m2. Bookings are accepted only within these physical limits.

6. Vehicle fill is limited by weight and floor positions together. Trailers carry 22,000 kg on 33 positions and therefore at most 27 full-weight pallets of 800 kg including load. The van carries 1,200 kg on 6 positions and therefore at most one full-weight pallet. The maximum dispatch promise per shift is 324 full-weight pallets, calculated as 12 loads multiplied by 27 pallets.

7. The 324-pallet figure is a binding promise limit for one shift. The dispatcher and shift supervisor confirm before release that booked pallets for the shift do not exceed 324 full-weight equivalents and that Zone D staging of 900 m2, wrapper output and scanner-confirmed labour cover the plan. Plans exceeding the limit, or inbound volumes exceeding Zone A clearance, are split across shifts before confirmation to the Client.

8. Cut-off times are applied per shift to protect booking, put-away, replenishment and release sequence. Inbound notifications with booking reference, quantities, product identities and batch or expiry data must arrive in time for dispatcher slot confirmation for the requested shift. Outbound orders must arrive in time for picking, packing, wrapping, staging in Zone D and dispatcher release within the same shift.

9. Orders and notifications received after the agreed cut-off for a shift are not promised for that shift. Harborwick rolls them to the next working shift in dispatcher sequence, confirms the revised slot, door and load to the Client, and stages only against the revised release. Early, late or unannounced arrivals wait for revised dispatcher instruction and do not displace booked loads.

10. Cut-off discipline applies equally to chilled goods for Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C and hazmat for the 60 m2 cage subject to 4,000 kg. Pallets exceeding 800 kg including load, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label are excluded from throughput and cut-off promises, held as pending or quarantined the same day under PR-09, and reported as exceptions with the shift confirmation.

title: Picking and Packing Accuracy
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. picks customer orders only in Zone C — picking of 1,200 m2, within the Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. No picking is promised in Zone A, B, D, E or F, and no order is picked from reserve stock, quarantine, returns pending inspection or the Zone F hazmat cage.

2. Pick faces are replenished before each picking shift under PR-03. Standard faces are fed exclusively from Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, chilled faces exclusively from Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C. No picking task starts on a face flagged as empty, blocked or unreleased, and open replenishment from the previous shift is completed first.

3. Replenishment runs only against active WMS tasks released by the stock controllers or shift supervisor. Forklift operators scan-verify source in Zone B or E and target face or flow-rack rear lane on handheld scanners. Only the tasked quantity is brought forward, faces are never overfilled or double-occupied, and reserve pallets are never staged in front picking aisles.

4. Order picking runs only against active WMS scanner tasks under PR-04. The 10 pickers work with the 20 shared handheld scanners, one task at a time, following scanner sequence by location, product, quantity and batch or expiry where applicable. Tasks are never split, reordered or shared without shift supervisor instruction.

5. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. The picker scans the face or lane label, then scans each item or carton label and confirms quantity. The system blocks mismatched product, wrong batch, over-pick and short-pick. Unscanned, unscannable or manually counted items are never forwarded to packing or Zone D.

6. First-in, first-out rotation is mandatory. Flow racks are loaded from the rear and picked only from the front in lane order, ground faces are picked from the indicated stock, and only the batch directed by the scanner is picked. Expired, damaged, mislabelled or unreadable stock is not picked, is segregated and reported, and goes to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

7. Short picks are controlled, not forced. If the tasked quantity is not available, the face is empty or the scanner flags zero stock, picking for that line stops, the short pick is recorded on the scanner and the lane is left clear. Harborwick informs the Client with the order confirmation and triggers second count and replenishment review before re-tasking.

8. Packing and labelling run under PR-05 by order, line, Client and delivery. Packing staff accept only scan-verified picks closed on the scanner, pack with batch separation where directed, and prohibit mixed orders, mixed batches and loose stacking. Every outbound pallet and carton carries a readable system label checked against the task for Client, product, quantity, destination and door.

9. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Overweight, unstable, overhanging or damaged builds are not dispatched. Every dispatch pallet is wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers to a stable, transport-safe standard without obscuring labels, and only wrapped and labelled pallets are handed for staging to Zone D. Packaging waste is removed to the cardboard baler.

10. Picking and packing accuracy is confirmed by scan and reported by shift. Completed picks are closed line by line with location, quantity, time and picker identity, packed pallets are confirmed with order, pallet identity, time and operator identity, and short picks, blocked faces, label faults and quarantine transfers are recorded by order and reported to the Client with the outbound confirmation and carried under PR-15 until resolved.

title: Put-away and Storage Accuracy
text:
1. Harborwick puts away only goods that have been booked into the warehouse management system in Zone A under PR-01. Uncounted, uninspected, unbooked, damaged or quarantined goods are never put away and never promised as available stock. No pallet leaves Zone A without a released put-away task under PR-02.

2. Every put-away task links one booked pallet to one recorded destination. Standard packed goods go to Zone B bulk storage of 2,200 m2 with 2,400 pallet positions. Chilled goods go directly to Zone E between +2 °C and +8 °C. Hazmat goes only to the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F. Zone C, Zone D and returns or value-added areas are never used as put-away destinations.

3. Collection from Zone A is prompt and in task sequence to keep Zone A clear for the next booked carrier at doors 1-4. Forklift operators scan-verify pallet label and source lane before lifting, transport by the 4.0 m main aisles, and scan-verify target bay or position on handheld scanners. Pallets without release stay under inbound control in Zone A.

4. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Pallets exceeding 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged or without a readable label are excluded from put-away and storage promises. Harborwick holds such pallets as pending in Zone A, reports the exception to the Client, and moves damaged goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg, including pallets and loads. This limit applies to every bay at every height and is built on the 800 kg pallet standard. Harborwick never overloads, double-occupies or uses rack positions for staging, and scan-verifies beam and bay labels on every placement. Bay limits are never overridden to clear Zone A or meet a shift target.

6. Free block-stacking outside the racking is permitted only in marked Zone B block areas and is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m height together.
