Stacks are vertical, aligned and stable on sound pallets of the same footprint. Leaning, mixed-footprint, damaged or overheight stacks are prohibited, are broken down immediately, and are reported as exceptions.

7. Chilled put-away is prioritised and direct under PR-12. Chilled pallets are collected first, moved without intermediate staging in Zone B, C or D, and confirmed in Zone E with cold-chain evidence intact. Pallets with broken evidence, damaged insulation or missing batch or expiry data are not stored as available and are segregated for Client instruction.

8. Hazmat put-away is direct and segregated under PR-13. Hazmat pallets move directly from Zone A to the cage without staging elsewhere and never on the same movement as food, drugstore or chilled goods. Total cage storage never exceeds 4,000 kg, which is at most 5 full-weight pallets. No task is released that would exceed the limit, and excess receipts are held for refusal or rebooking.

9. Storage accuracy means the stock in the system is the stock on the rack. Every placement and removal is scan-verified by source and target with time and operator identity, and every pallet has one system location. Reserve stock in Zone B and Zone E is never picked directly; replenishment to Zone C runs only against active tasks before each picking shift.

10. Put-away and storage status is reported by shift and carried under PR-15. Completed and uncompleted tasks, blocked bays, overweight or damaged holds, cage weight against the 4,000 kg limit, Zone E temperature status and quarantine transfers are recorded by pallet and location and reported to the Client with the stock and inbound confirmations until every booked pallet has a known location or resolved exception.

title: Cycle Counts, Stocktake and Reporting
text:
1. Harborwick runs cycle counts every working day, Monday to Friday, on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08. Counting never stops: each working day a defined part of Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone and the Zone F cage and quarantine is counted, so that all Client locations are covered in rotation.

2. Daily counts are owned by the 2 stock controllers and run only against active WMS scanner tasks. Counters scan the location label, then scan each pallet and carton label and confirm quantity, product, batch or expiry on the 20 shared handheld scanners. Manual estimates, unscanned quantities and counts from memory are never used and never reported as stock.

3. Only inspected and booked stock is reported as available. Quarantine in Zone F, returns pending inspection, hazmat against the 4,000 kg limit and any pallet held in Zone A awaiting booking are counted separately as blocked or unavailable. Empty faces, zero-stock flags and double occupations are confirmed on the scanner and reported as exceptions.

4. Every count is reconciled immediately against the warehouse management system: the stock in the system is the stock on the rack. Matches are closed with location, quantity, time and counter identity. Any difference stops closure for that location, the location is physically secured and marked for recount, and no put-away, replenishment or picking continues there until cleared.

5. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. A different counter from the first count recounts the secured location independently, re-scans all labels and confirms unit of measure, batch and expiry. Only a confirmed difference is prepared as an adjustment with cause, quantity, value and both counter identities. Unconfirmed differences are recounted again until resolved.

6. Once a year Harborwick shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake under PR-08. All receiving at doors 1-4, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing and dispatch at doors 5-8 are stopped. Every stocked location in Zone B, Zone C, Zone E, the 60 m2 cage, quarantine, returns inspection stock and any booked pallets in Zone A or Zone D is counted in one continuous count. No location is carried forward from cycle counts.

7. The wall-to-wall stocktake is prepared and led by the stock controllers with independent count teams on scanner tasks. Damaged, expired or suspect goods found are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Racking evidence against the 2,700 kg bay limit and the 3-high and 4.0 m block limit is checked and blocked where required.

8. The stocktake result becomes binding only with the signature of the warehouse manager. Harborwick presents full counts, second counts, recounts and prepared adjustments by zone and value. No stocktake adjustment is posted to the system, and no write-off above 500 EUR is applied, without this sign-off. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case.

9. Racking accuracy is protected by documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects uprights, beams, locks, bracing and labels across Zone B, Zone C and Zone E, and every repair is logged. Impacted, deformed or overloaded bays are blocked, unloaded if required, and excluded from availability until cleared and reported.

10. Harborwick reports inventory control by shift and by event. Daily counts completed, locations blocked for recount, adjustments prepared and awaiting approval, quarantine transfers and Zone E and cage status are recorded by location and reported to the Client with the stock confirmations and carried under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00 until resolved. Annual stocktake results, approved adjustments and remaining blocks are reported in the closing stocktake statement.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Harborwick quarantines all damaged, suspect, expired and non-conforming Client goods the same day they are found, under PR-09. This applies whether damage is found in Zone A, B, C, D, E or F, during receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch, cycle counts or returns inspection. No damaged pallet is carried to the next shift unsecured.

2. Quarantine is located only in the marked quarantine area in Zone F. No quarantine stock is held in Zone A, Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone D staging, Zone E cold zone, the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage, transit lanes or the yard. Any damaged pallet found outside quarantine is secured, marked and moved the same day.

3. Quarantined pallets are physically separated, clearly marked with cause, date, source zone and finder identity, and system-blocked as not available in the warehouse management system on handheld scanners. Blocked stock is never picked, replenished, packed, staged in Zone D, loaded or reported as available until a disposition decision is recorded and reported to the Client.

4. The finder secures the area and reports immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. The shift supervisor confirms segregation and system blocking, initiates incident review, and directs spill response under PR-13 for hazmat or cleaning and cold-chain hold under PR-12 for chilled goods between +2 °C and +8 °C. The area stays secured until cleared.

5. Inspection of quarantined goods takes place only in Zone F and only by returns and packing staff, with every unit inspected individually without sampling. Quantity, product, batch or expiry, value and cause are recorded on WMS scanners with time and operator identity. Uninspected, unscanned or manually estimated units are never released for decision.

6. Final disposition is restock, rework or scrap. Only units in original, intact, clean, correctly labelled and in-date condition with full traceability are released back via booking to Zone B, Zone E or the cage. Rework runs only in value-added packing in Zone F with re-inspection. All other units remain blocked for scrap and disposal, and no restock, rework or scrap takes place without recorded shift supervisor approval.

7. Write-off authority follows the fixed 500 EUR threshold per case. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case. Any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold, and no write-off above 500 EUR is applied without manager sign-off.

8. Every write-off is documented with cause, quantity, value, delivery or location reference, both count identities and approval identity, and reported to the Client with the incident and stock confirmations. Damaged goods found during daily cycle counts or the annual wall-to-wall stocktake are quarantined the same day, and no adjustment is posted without a second count by a different counter.

9. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg in quarantine movements. Overweight, unstable, overhanging, leaking or unreadable pallets are not stacked, not block-stacked above 3 high and 4.0 m, and not placed in racking. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, hazmat quarantine respects the 4,000 kg cage limit of at most 5 full-weight pallets, and incompatible goods are never placed together.

10. Harborwick reports quarantine status by shift and by event. Every placement, inspection result, disposition proposal, approval, write-off and disposal is recorded with time and operator identity, reported to the Client with the shift confirmations, and carried with clear ownership under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00 until resolved. Open quarantine, stock held as unavailable and write-offs awaiting approval are never closed silently.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Returns Inspection and Disposition
text:
1. Harborwick accepts Client returns only in Zone F under PR-07 and only within 14 days of delivery. The 14-day count runs from the documented delivery date to the date the goods physically arrive back on site. Returns arriving after 14 days are refused, held segregated, and reported to the Client for clarification before any handling.

2. All returns arrive only on a prior booking confirmed by the dispatcher, with a specific door and fixed time slot at doors 1-4, inbound only. Drivers report at the yard entrance, wait only in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard, and never enter the hall or Zone F. Drivers take no part in unloading, inspection or decision.

3. Unloading is performed by trained inbound and returns staff with pallet jacks and the electric fleet at the 1.2 m door with leveller. Unloaded return pallets remain under control in Zone A reception lanes only for transfer and are moved promptly to the marked returns inspection area in Zone F. No return is restocked, reworked or dispatched on arrival.

4. Every return is system-blocked as not available on receipt in the warehouse management system on handheld WMS scanners. Blocked returns are never placed on pick faces in Zone C, in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, in Zone E, or in Zone D staging, and are never picked, packed or reported as available until a disposition is approved.

5. Inspection takes place only in the marked returns area in Zone F and only by the 4 returns and packing staff under the shift supervisor. Inspection starts only after delivery reference, Client, original delivery date, quantity and reason for return are recorded. Every returned unit is inspected individually, without sampling, and unscanned or manually estimated units are never forwarded.

6. Inspection covers packaging integrity, sealing, labelling, batch and expiry data, contamination, damage and signs of use or tampering, with cold-chain evidence checked for chilled goods between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12 and labelling, closure and leakage checked for hazmat under PR-13. Chilled returns are moved without delay with minimum exposure time, hazmat returns move directly under the 60 m2 cage procedure without staging in Zone B, C, D or E.

7. For every inspected unit Harborwick proposes the disposition and records it by return, pallet, product, quantity and finding: restock to available stock, rework in value-added packing, or scrap. Only intact, clean, correctly labelled and in-date units with full traceability are proposed for restock, with cold-chain and hazmat evidence intact. Repairable outer faults are proposed for rework with re-inspection, all other damaged, expired or non-conforming units are proposed for scrap.

8. No restock, rework or scrap takes place without recorded approval of the final disposition by the shift supervisor under PR-07 and PR-09. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming units go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found, physically separated, marked and system-blocked. Approved restock is booked via the system only to Zone B, Zone E or the ventilated cage subject to the 4,000 kg limit, never directly to Zone C or Zone D.

9. Write-off authority follows the fixed 500 EUR threshold per case. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR per case, any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager. No case is split to stay below the threshold. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg on any restock, rework or scrap movement.

10. Harborwick reports returns status by shift and by event. Every receipt, inspection result, proposal, approval, restock booking, rework order, scrap transfer, write-off and disposal is recorded with time and operator identity, reported to the Client with the shift confirmations, and carried with clear ownership under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00 until resolved. Units awaiting approval, rework in progress and scrap awaiting disposal are never closed silently.

chapter_title: Damaged Goods, Returns and Chilled Storage
title: Temperature-Controlled Storage
text:
1. Harborwick provides chilled storage only in Zone E — cold zone of 300 m2, within the Monday to Friday shifts 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00. Zone E holds only inspected and booked chilled packed goods requiring +2 °C to +8 °C. No ambient goods, hazmat, quarantine, returns or value-added work is placed in Zone E, and no chilled Client goods are stored in Zone A, B, C, D or F.

2. The temperature in Zone E is held between +2 °C and +8 °C at all times. This commits cooling operation on both shifts, during pre-agreed Saturday morning overtime in peak season and outside operating hours. Cooling units, doors, curtains, seals and sensors are kept closed and serviceable, and doors are opened only for an active put-away, replenishment or counting task and closed immediately afterwards.

3. Zone E is equipped with continuous temperature monitoring and alarms under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Any alarm, deviation outside +2 °C to +8 °C, cooling, door, sensor or power fault is acted on immediately, the shift supervisor is informed, affected stock is secured and system-blocked as not available, and no chilled pallet is picked, replenished, packed, staged or reported as available until cleared.

4. A manual temperature verification is performed in Zone E on each shift. The morning shift and the afternoon shift each record reading, time, device identity and operator identity, reviewed and countersigned by the shift supervisor. A missing or failed verification stops all chilled put-away, replenishment, picking and counting, and Harborwick reports the hold to the Client until a verified reading back in range is recorded.

5. Chilled put-away is prioritised and direct under PR-02 and PR-12. Chilled pallets are booked in Zone A only after document check, count and inspection with cold-chain evidence checked, collected first, and moved directly to Zone E without intermediate staging in Zone B, C or D and without joint transport with hazmat or damaged goods. Exposure time outside the cold zone is kept to the minimum.

6. Chilled replenishment to Zone C runs only against active WMS tasks before each picking shift under PR-03. Only the tasked quantity leaves Zone E for the assigned chilled face, exposure time is kept to the minimum, and pallets not placed are returned to Zone E without delay. Chilled goods leave Zone E only for ordered replenishment, cycle counts or approved quarantine transfer.

7. A pallet, load included, may weigh at most 800 kg. Pallets exceeding 800 kg, unstable, overhanging, damaged, with broken cold-chain evidence, damaged insulation, or missing batch, expiry or readable labels are excluded from chilled availability promises. Harborwick segregates such pallets, reports the exception to the Client, and moves damaged goods to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

8. Damaged, expired, suspect or cold-chain-broken chilled goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. They are physically separated, clearly marked, system-blocked as not available on handheld scanners, and never picked, packed, staged in Zone D or reported as available. Chilled returns are handled only in Zone F with minimum exposure time and intact-evidence check before any restock proposal.

9. Every placement and removal in Zone E is scan-verified by source and target on handheld WMS scanners, with time and operator identity, using only assigned labelled chilled positions. Aisles, evaporators, sensors and emergency equipment are kept clear, trucks and jacks used in Zone E are clean, dry and free of contamination, and condensation, spillage and ice are cleaned, secured and reported immediately.

10. Harborwick reports cold-chain status by shift and by event. Every reading, alarm, deviation, quarantine transfer and open chilled task is recorded by pallet and location, reported to the Client with the stock and shift confirmations, and carried with clear ownership under PR-15 at 14:00 and 22:00 until resolved. Last verified temperature, alarm status, stock held as unavailable and pallets awaiting put-away are never closed silently.
